title: Proof of a Conjecture of Matherne, Morales, and Selover on Encodings of Unit Interval Orders
abstractText: There are two bijections from unit interval orders on $n$ elements to Dyck paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$. One is to consider the pairs of incomparable elements as forming the set of boxes between a Dyck path and the diagonal. Another is to find a particular part listing (in the sense of Guay-Paquet, Rowland and Morales) which yields an isomorphic poset, and to interpret the part listing as the area sequence of a Dyck path. Matherne, Morales, and Selover conjectured that, for any unit interval order, these two Dyck paths are related by Haglund's well-known zeta bijection. In this paper we prove their conjecture.

title: Local convergence of a proximal type method for weakly convex minimization
abstractText: Abstract The main purpose of this paper is to develop and analyze a proximal-type method for the local minimization of weakly convex functions. Our motivation for introducing this algorithm is to increase its versatility and applicability in a broader range of scenarios in optimization and introduce a more adaptable version of the method for typical generalizations. Our study relies heavily on the Moreau envelope, a well-known mathematical tool used to analyze the behavior of the proximal operator. By leveraging the properties of the Moreau envelope, we are able to prove that the proximal algorithm converges in local contexts. Moreover, we present a complexity result to assess the practical feasibility of the proximal algorithm and provide a numerical example to illustrate the practical behavior of the algorithm.

title: POISSON TRANSFORMS, THE BGG COMPLEX AND DISCRETE SERIES REPRESENTATIONS OF S U ( n + 1 , 1 ) $SU(n+1,1)$ upper S upper U left parenthesis n plus 1 comma 1 right parenthesis
abstractText: Abstract The aim of this article is to construct specific Poisson transforms mapping differential forms on the sphere S 2 n + 1 $S^{2n+1}$ upper S Superscript 2 n plus 1 endowed with its natural CR structure to forms on complex hyperbolic space. These transforms have coclosed harmonic values, descend to the BGG (Rumin) complex, and intertwine the differential operators in that complex with the exterior derivative. Passing to the Poincaré ball model, we analyze boundary asymptotics, proving that the values of our transforms admit a continuous extension to the boundary in degrees ≤ n $\leq n$ less than or equals n . Finally, we show that, composing the exterior derivative with the transform in degree n , one obtains an isomorphism between the kernel of the Rumin operator in degree n and a dense subspace of the L 2 $L^2$ upper L squared -harmonic forms on complex hyperbolic space. This provides a realization of the discrete series representations of S U ( n + 1 , 1 ) $SU(n+1,1)$ upper S upper U left parenthesis n plus 1 comma 1 right parenthesis with trivial infinitesimal character in spaces of differential forms on the compact manifold S 2 n + 1 $S^{2n+1}$ upper S Superscript 2 n plus 1 . These developments are motivated by a programme of the third author to prove some instances of the Baum-Connes conjecture. The first part of the article is valid in a much more general setting; in particular, it is relevant for cases in which the conjecture is still open.

title: An Extended Generalization of RSK Correspondence via $A$ Type Quiver Representations
abstractText: Let $\lambda=(\lambda_1 \geqslant \ldots \geqslant \lambda_k > 0)$. For any $c$ Coxeter element of $\mathfrak{S}_{\lambda_1+k}$, we construct a bijection from fillings of $\lambda$ to reverse plane partitions. We recover two previous generalizations of the Robinson-Schensted-Knuth correspondence for particular choices of Coxeter element depending on $\lambda$: one based on the work of, among others, Burge, Hillman, Grassl, Knuth, and uniformly presented by Gansner; the other developed by Garver, Partrias, and Thomas, and independently by Dauvergne, called Scrambled RSK. Our results in this paper develop the combinatorial consequence of our previous work of type $A_{\lambda_1+k-1}$ quivers.

title: Size of Multipartitions through Level-Rank Duality
abstractText: We give short purely combinatorial proofs for certain formulae relating the size of an $l$-partition with the one of its $e$-quotient in the sense of Uglov. We deduce a way to compute the size of the $e$-core of multipartitions and the $e$-weight of a multipartition. All these multipartitions naturally appear in the context of level-rank duality for Ariki-Koike algebras and Cherednik algebras.

title: Role of phycospheric bacteria: Promoting the growth of Isochrysis zhanjiangensis and ammonia nitrogen removal in rearing water
abstractText: Isochrysis zhanjiangensis is crucial in the breeding of bivalves larval as an artificially cultivated feed microalga. To investigate their roles in algal–bacterial interactions, we isolated and identified two phycospheric bacterial strains, Halomonas piezotolerans and Alteromonas abrolhosensis, from I. zhanjiangensis and examined their effects on algal growth and ammonia nitrogen removal in aquaculture systems. The results indicated that both bacterial strains promoted the growth of I. zhanjiangensis; however, the effect of A. abrolhosensis was more pronounced. At a concentration of 108 cfu/mL, the A. abrolhosensis treatment group reached a cell density of 1.082 × 107 cells/mL on day 10, significantly higher than the control group by 16.26% (p < 0.05). The chlorophyll a content was 4.99 μg/L, representing a 43.8% increase compared to the control group (p < 0.05), and the total polysaccharide content was 8.366 g/L, significantly higher by 59.9% (p < 0.05). H. piezotolerans at a concentration of 106 cfu/mL increased the soluble protein content, with the co-culture group showing a 4.65% increase (p > 0.05). Furthermore, H. piezotolerans enhanced soluble protein synthesis at low concentrations. In ammonia nitrogen removal experiments, H. piezotolerans showed superior and stable activity, while A. abrolhosensis also promoted nitrogen reduction. The qPCR validation revealed upregulation of nirB and nosZ genes in H. piezotolerans, and enhanced expression of nirB, glnG, glnL, and glnA genes in A. abrolhosensis, confirming their ammonia nitrogen removal potential. This study demonstrates that phycospheric bacteria isolated from I. zhanjiangensis promote algal growth and facilitate ammonia nitrogen removal during bivalves larval rearing. These results provide new insights into bacteria–algae interactions and indicate practical implications for enhancing algal productivity and maintaining environmental stability in hatchery systems.

title: Unexpectedly, a Symmetry on Unlabeled Graphs
abstractText: We exhibit the joint symmetric distribution of the following two parameters on the set of unlabeled simple connected graphs with $n$ vertices. The first parameter is the maximal number of leaves attached to a vertex. The second parameter is the size of the largest set of vertices sharing the same closed neighborhood minus $1$. Apparently, this is the first example of a natural non-trivial equidistribution of graph parameters on unlabeled simple connected graphs with a fixed set of vertices. Our proof is enumerative, using the theory of species. Exhibiting an explicit bijection interchanging the two parameters remains an open problem.

title: Freespace “twistronics”: moiré structured light for optical supertopologies
abstractText: Abstract Moiré superlattices of twisted bilayer 2D materials creating nontrivial physical effects have recently revolutionized diverse subjects across materials, optoelectronics, nanophotonics, and beyond. Here, we present moiré superlattices in higher-dimensional freespace optics, where the basic twisted lattice is not a layer of 2D material, but a propagating structured light field with periodic topological textures. The moiré structured light with flexibly tuned twist angle can generate and transit among a rich set of topologies, including skyrmionium bags, skyrmion bag superlattices, skyrmion clusters, and quasicrystals, with controlled symmetry, most of which were not discovered in any other systems. Importantly, our freespace moiré textures maintain their topologies over long-distance propagation with nondiffractive behavior and topological robustness against perturbations and obstacles. Our work unlocks higher dimensions of moiré photonics to manipulate super-resilient topologies and address the challenges of robust information transfer and encryption.

title: Educational framework to strengthen the variant scientist workforce in clinical genomics
abstractText: Abstract Background The integration of genomics into clinical care has created an urgent need for accurate, standardized variant interpretation. Variant scientists (VS) play a central role in translating sequencing results into clinically actionable findings, yet no formal framework currently supports their professional development. We surveyed practicing VS to identify training routes and knowledge gaps and used these insights to design a training program. Methods A national survey delivered to every practicing VS assessed training background, learning, access to interpretation tools, and professional challenges. A multidisciplinary committee defined core competencies and developed a phased training program. Results Thirty-eight respondents were included. Professional training was mostly acquired through observation of expert analysts (42.1%), followed by hands-on experience (39.5%). Only 18% participated in a dedicated VS course. Key challenges included keeping pace with evolving guidelines (55.2%) and copy number variant (CNV) analysis (47.3%). To help narrow these gaps and support more unified VS training, we developed a comprehensive framework combining theoretical modules, practical rotations, and assessment via a standardized proficiency test, supported by institutional forums and national meetings. Conclusion We deigned a unified, scalable VS training model to address core educational gaps and support standardization of variant interpretation training nationally and internationally.

title: Mission-aware Model Predictive Control for tactical microgrids under monsoon uncertainty
abstractText: Tactical microgrids in remote and mission-critical environments must ensure reliable power, reduce fuel use, and maintain acoustic stealth under uncertain renewable generation. However, most existing control strategies are either rule-based or single-objective, which limits their ability to handle these conflicting goals in real time.This paper proposes a mission-aware Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for a hybrid PV–battery–diesel microgrid. The approach directly embeds mission priorities into the dispatch problem using a rolling-horizon optimization. A key novelty is the Survival Override mechanism, which protects battery reserves under solar forecast uncertainty and helps prevent mission failure.The framework is validated through co-simulation using Python and DIgSILENT PowerFactory with realistic solar data. The results show a 61.9% reduction in fuel consumption compared to conventional control. At the same time, the system maintains voltage stability and supports up to 20 hours of continuous silent operation. The controller also handles forecast errors of up to 15% through 15-minute receding horizon updates, avoiding early battery depletion and inefficient generator use.Overall, the proposed approach improves microgrid resilience, reduces fuel logistics, and enhances operational performance without requiring additional system capacity.

title: How the wear of WC and PCBN inserts affects the surface integrity of Inconel 718 in dry, flood and cryogenic finish turning
abstractText: Aerospace components must adhere to extremely stringent reliability standards, necessitating the use of high-performance alloys such as Inconel 718. While valued for its superior mechanical properties across a wide temperature range, Inconel 718 is notoriously difficult to machine, often resulting in rapid tool wear and compromised surface integrity. Furthermore, Inconel 718 is usually machined using conventional flood lubrication, which poses sustainability challenges and high disposal costs. This study has the twofold objective of (i) evaluating the feasibility of dry and cryogenic finishing turning as eco-friendly alternatives to traditional flood lubrication, and (ii) assessing the performance of polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) inserts compared to traditional coated tungsten carbide (WC) ones. Tool wear and surface roughness were continuously monitored until the inserts’ end-of-life, while surface integrity was evaluated at the end of the inserts’ life for each cutting condition investigated. Results indicate that the dominant wear mechanisms of WC inserts were abrasion and adhesion under all tested lubrication-cooling conditions, although cryogenic cooling slightly extended their life, yielding smoother, higher-quality surfaces with reduced severe deformation layer at the same time. Although PCBN inserts exhibited shorter tool life than WC inserts, they showed comparable lifetimes under dry and flood conditions, with cryogenic cooling yielding the highest surface quality and the thinnest SPD layer. While lubrication strategies and cutting speeds significantly influenced surface characteristics, all tested conditions met aerospace standards, confirming the industrial viability of sustainable machining strategies for Inconel 718.

title: Macrophage-derived migrasomes promote fibrotic remodeling in endometriosis with TGF-β/Smad signaling activation
abstractText: Abstract Background Progressive fibrosis of ectopic lesions is a major pathological feature of endometriosis, contributing to treatment resistance and disease recurrence. However, the mechanisms driving this fibrotic process remain incompletely understood. Methods A murine model of endometriosis was established by transplanting endometrial tissue fragments into the peritoneal cavity of C57BL/6 mice. Macrophage-derived migrasomes were isolated from cultured RAW264.7 cells, characterized by scanning electron microscopy and Western blot, and administered intraperitoneally to endometriosis-bearing mice. Fibrotic changes were assessed by histology, immunofluorescence, and Western blot analysis of signaling pathways and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers. Cytokine levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results Exogenously administered macrophage-derived migrasomes accumulated at ectopic lesion sites and markedly aggravated fibrotic remodeling. Migrasome-treated lesions exhibited cyst-wall thickening, increased stromal cellularity, and extensive collagen deposition. At the molecular level, migrasome treatment was associated with activation of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)/Smad pathway in ectopic lesions, as indicated by increased phosphorylation of Smad2 and Smad3 without significant changes in total Smad2/3 levels. This was accompanied by increased α-smooth muscle actin and vimentin expression together with reduced cytokeratin 18 (CK18) and E-cadherin expression, consistent with EMT-like phenotypic reprogramming. In parallel, TGF-β1 and VEGF levels were elevated, whereas MMP9 was reduced, collectively supporting a pro-fibrotic microenvironment. Conclusions These findings identify macrophage-derived migrasomes as previously unrecognized promoters of fibrotic remodeling in endometriosis and support a role for migrasome-associated signaling in lesion progression. This work provides new insight into the pathogenesis of endometriosis-associated fibrosis and highlights migrasomes as a potential target for future anti-fibrotic intervention.

title: Environmental influences on physical activity among young rural women: a qualitative study
abstractText: Abstract Background Environmental factors, including the built and social environments, shape physical activity. However, it is less clear how young rural women experience these influences in daily life. This study aimed to understand perceived barriers and facilitators to active lifestyles. Methods A descriptive qualitative design was used to explore environmental influences on physical activity among young rural women. Nineteen participants completed individual semi-structured interviews. Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Results Four main themes were identified: the built environment, natural and geographic environment, structural environment, and social environment. Participants mainly described barriers, such as limited access to facilities, transportation challenges, cost, poor infrastructure, safety concerns, social support and weather-related issues. Conclusion Rural environments can limit physical activity for young women but also offer support for active lifestyles. These findings highlight the need to address barriers and to leverage existing support in rural communities. This study may help guide targeted strategies to promote physical activity among young rural women.

title: A New Group in the Riordan Family of Matrix Groups: the Sprugnoli Group
abstractText: We define a group of lower-triangular matrices whose columns are defined by power series. This group can be seen as a generalization of the (ordinary) Riordan group and the double Riordan group. Elements of this group are defined by three power series. Sequence bisections and vertically stretched Riordan arrays play an important role in the formulation of this group. We give a production matrix characterization of this new group. We have chosen to name this group in memory of Renzo Sprugnoli, who was a pioneer in the application of the Riordan group to combinatorial problems as well as contributing to an understanding of the rich structure of Riordan arrays. We indicate how higher order groups can be defined, based on $n$-tuples of power series and $n$-sections of sequences that they operate on.

title: Municipal spending on school health services is unequally associated with dual-factor mental health profiles: a latent profile study of 63,000 Swedish adolescents, 2006–2024
abstractText: Abstract Background Adolescent mental health has declined internationally, prompting increased investment in school-based services. However, whether such investments benefit all students equally remains unclear. We examined whether municipal spending on school mental health services is differentially associated with dual-factor mental health profiles, which distinguish psychiatric symptoms from subjective well-being, among Swedish adolescents. Methods Data were drawn from Stockholmsenkäten (the Stockholm Survey), a biennial population-based survey of 9th-grade students (approximately 15 years) in Region Stockholm, Sweden. The analytic sample comprised 63 190 students across 26 municipalities surveyed between 2006 and 2024. Latent profile analysis identified four mental health profiles based on psychiatric symptoms and school well-being: Complete Mental Health, Troubled (high symptoms, low well-being), Vulnerable (low symptoms, low well-being), and Symptomatic but Content (high symptoms, adequate well-being). Municipal spending on school health services (per student, lagged two years) was decomposed into within-municipality (year-to-year change) and between-municipality (stable differences) components. Multilevel multinomial logistic regression estimated associations between spending and profile membership, controlling for gender and secular trends. Results Complete Mental Health declined from 55.6% (2006) to 45.4% (2024), while the Troubled profile more than doubled (3.4% to 7.2%). The Vulnerable profile remained stable at approximately 17%. Within-municipality spending increases were associated with 16% lower odds of the Troubled profile (OR = 0.84, 95% CI 0.73–0.95, p = .007) but showed no significant association with the Vulnerable profile (OR = 1.08, 95% CI 0.99–1.17, p = .084). Spending was associated with 9% higher odds of the Symptomatic but Content profile (OR = 1.09, 95% CI 1.01–1.17, p = .026), possibly reflecting transitions from Troubled to Symptomatic. Conclusions Increased investment in school mental health services appears protective for students with visible psychiatric symptoms but does not reach those whose struggles manifest as low well-being without psychiatric symptoms. From a precision public health perspective, current service models may require reorientation to identify and support the Vulnerable subgroup, who comprise one in six adolescents and remain unaffected by spending increases.

title: Age and DRE-assessed anal sphincter tone are associated with vasovagal reactions during transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy
abstractText: Abstract Objective To identify clinically accessible predictors of vasovagal reactions during TRUS-guided prostate biopsy, with particular emphasis on age and anal sphincter strength assessed during digital rectal examination. Methods Clinical data from 663 patients who underwent transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy between May 2022 and May 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were categorized into vasovagal reaction and non-vasovagal reaction groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of vasovagal reactions, and model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Results Vasovagal reactions occurred in 30 patients (4.52%). Multivariate analysis identified age < 65 years (OR = 6.006, 95% CI: 2.379–15.165) and grade 3 anal sphincter contraction strength (OR = 16.484, 95% CI: 4.910–55.344) as independent predictors. A predictive model incorporating these factors demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an area under the curve of 0.846 (95% CI: 0.781–0.912). Conclusion Age and elevated anal sphincter contraction strength are significant predictors of vasovagal reactions during transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy. Pre-procedural identification of these features may facilitate risk stratification and enable targeted preventive strategies to enhance procedural safety.

title: Chalcogen-Controlled Triplet Harvesting in Benzophenone-Derived Chromophores: A Theoretical Investigation of Excited-State Relaxation Pathways
abstractText: Abstract Efficient triplet-state harvesting in organic chromophores is governed by a delicate interplay between excited-state energetics, orbital character, spin–orbit coupling, and vibronic coupling. Here, we present a systematic theoretical investigation of chalcogen substitution in benzophenone-derived chromophores, in which the carbonyl oxygen is progressively replaced by sulfur and selenium. Three molecular families were examined: benzophenone, Michler’s ketone, and 4,4′-dinitrobenzophenone, together with their thio- and seleno-analogues. Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT) calculations were used to characterize excited-state energetics, absorption and emission properties, natural transition orbitals (NTOs), spin–orbit coupling (SOC) matrix elements, quantitative hole–electron descriptors, interfragment charge-transfer character (IFCT), and state-specific intersystem-crossing (ISC) rates. Chalcogen substitution systematically stabilizes the low-lying excited states, produces pronounced red shifts in the lowest absorption bands, and reorganizes the singlet–triplet manifold. Simultaneously, the heavier chalcogen atoms markedly enhance SOC. For the strongest retained S1 → T2 SOC channels, the calculated SOC increases from 35.96 to 134.19 and 645.36 cm–1 across BP, TBP, and SBP, respectively, with analogous O → S → Se enhancements in the substituted series. Quantitative NTO, hole–electron, and IFCT analyses show that these SOC trends are coupled to excitation localization, hole–electron overlap, and charge-transfer character. NTO analysis reveals that the lowest singlet excited states are predominantly of (nπ*) character, whereas the higher triplet states relevant to strong SOC frequently possess substantial (ππ*) character, providing favorable El-Sayed-type spin-conversion pathways. The results therefore show that chalcogen identity, orbital-character change, and the spatial distribution of the participating excited states act cooperatively in controlling singlet–triplet coupling in these benzophenone-derived chromophores.

title: Preparation and properties of gel polymer electrolytes based on tetrafunctional cross-linked PEG network
abstractText: Abstract Thiol-yne click reaction between pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) and α, ω-dipropiolate-terminated polyethylene glycol was carried out in propylene carbonate containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imideto obtain gel polymer electrolyte with tetra-branched network structure. The ionic conductivity was found to depend on the polymer content in the gel polymer electrolyte and the chain length of the polyethylene glycol constituting the tetra-branched network structure. These experimental results indicated that lithium cations moved not only within the electrolyte solution but also along the PEG chains that form a network structure.

title: QuatHashing: perceptual hashing with quaternion discrete wavelet transform for reduced-reference visual security assessment
abstractText: Abstract Visual security assessment (VSA) is an important task of perceptual image encryption and plays a key role in evaluating the effectiveness of encryption schemes. This paper proposes a perceptual hashing algorithm with quaternion discrete wavelet transform (QDWT) for reduced-reference (RR) VSA. The directional complementary sub-band representation is exploited to reorganize the image into horizontal and vertical complementary sub-bands. Since the pixel rearrangement does not discard any information, the distortion introduced by encryption is preserved in the complementary sub-bands while the directional image information is explicitly represented. The complementary sub-bands are modeled as two pure quaternion images and decomposed by QDWT to extract perceptually relevant features from the horizontal and vertical channels. The low-frequency structural features, texture features and multi-scale structural features are further obtained to describe the residual visual information from both directional and multi-scale perspectives. As the human eye is more sensitive to visually salient regions, global and local attention mechanisms are introduced to emphasize these regions and generate compact perceptual feature sequences. The perceptual hash is finally determined by quantizing and combining the horizontal and vertical feature sequences, and the Euclidean distance between the hashes of the reference and encrypted images is used as the final visual security score. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed QuatHashing achieves more consistent performance than existing IQA and VSA methods, particularly for encrypted images with low and moderate visual quality.

title: Screening for paternal perinatal affective symptoms: psychometric properties of the Perinatal Assessment of Paternal Affectivity (PAPA 2.0) in the Polish context
abstractText: Paternal perinatal mental health has been gaining considerable attention in contemporary scientific literature. Correlational and longitudinal associations have been established between paternal depressive and anxiety symptoms, maternal mental health and child development. Yet, we still lack assessment instruments tailored to fathers’ specific affective symptom profile that could prompt early detection and intervention. The present study examined the psychometric properties of the Polish adaptation of the Perinatal Assessment of Paternal Affectivity questionnaire (PAPA version 2.0), which represents a further development of PAPA tool published in 2022. The prenatal assessment included 213 fathers in the third trimester of their partners’ pregnancy, while 72 fathers participated in the postnatal phase. Reliability, concurrent validity, factorial structure and associations between prenatal and postnatal scores were evaluated. PAPA 2.0 demonstrated high internal consistency before and after childbirth. Its total scores showed moderate-to-high positive correlations with depressive symptoms, perceived stress, global psychological distress and postnatal EPDS scores, indicating satisfactory concurrent validity. Exploratory factor analysis suggested a two-factor structure with one item - describing risky behaviors - showing poor item discrimination, which may point to the need for this item’s reformulation in future studies. Prenatal and postnatal PAPA scores were significantly associated, suggesting relative stability of paternal affective symptoms across the perinatal period. The study is limited by its convenience sample, high educational and urban bias as well as pandemic-related substantial postnatal attrition. Despite these limitations, the findings support PAPA 2.0 as a promising screening tool for identifying paternal perinatal affective symptoms in Polish fathers.

title: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma pretreatment as a novel tool to tailor the functional properties of quince seed mucilage biopolymer-based edible films
abstractText: Abstract Background Quince seed mucilage (QSM) is a promising polysaccharide for the fabrication of biodegradable edible films; however, its relatively limited functional performance restricts broader food-packaging applications. Scope and Approach: The present study investigated the effects of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) treatment applied to QSM solutions at 6, 7, and 8 kV for 1, 3, and 5 min, followed by a comprehensive evaluation of the physicochemical, surface, barrier, mechanical, and thermal properties of the resulting films. Key Findings: CAP treatment did not significantly affect film thickness regardless of the applied processing conditions. Contact angle analysis demonstrated that the highest surface hydrophobicity was achieved under a 7 kV for 3 min plasma treatment. Water vapor barrier measurements revealed that films treated for 3 min exhibited the lowest permeability, irrespective of the applied voltage. Surface topography analysis indicated that 6 kV for 1min plasma exposure generated the greatest surface roughness, whereas increasing either the treatment duration or applied voltage produced a denser, more homogeneous, and compact film microstructure. Compared with the untreated control, CAP treatment significantly enhanced the mechanical performance of the films, with the optimum tensile properties obtained following treatment at 6 kV for 1 min. Thermal characterization by TGA and DSC further demonstrated that 5 min plasma exposure time adversely affected the thermal stability of the films, while optimized CAP conditions (3 min) provided the most favorable thermal performance. Conclusions Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriately optimized CAP treatment effectively improves the structural integrity and functional performance of QSM-based biodegradable films.

title: Peripheral immune profile of periodontitis patients and reduced expression of CD11b in periodontitis
abstractText: Abstract Background Periodontitis is an inflammatory disease caused by the complex interaction between plaque microorganisms and the host immune system that threatens oral health. Leukocyte recruitment plays important roles during the protective and pathological immune responses of many diseases, including periodontitis. CD14 and CD11b are adhesion molecules that promote adhesion of leukocytes to the vascular endothelium to defend against microorganisms. In this cross-sectional study, we aimed to determine the difference between the expression levels of CD14 and CD11b expressed on leukocytes and analyzed subclasses of lymphocytes in individuals with periodontitis compared to healthy individuals. Methods Fourteen periodontitis patients and fourteen healthy individuals were included in the study. Venous blood samples were collected from each individual. T lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry using peripheral blood mononuclear cells stained with anti-CD3, anti-CD4, and anti-CD8 antibodies. Natural killer (NK) cells and Natural killer T (NKT) cells were analyzed by flow cytometry using peripheral blood cells stained with anti-CD3, anti-CD16, and anti-CD56 antibodies. The monocyte adhesion molecule CD14 and the common leukocyte adhesion molecule CD11b were analyzed by flow cytometry. Results The proportions of NK and NKT cells were significantly higher in periodontitis patients than in healthy subjects (p < 0.05). CD11b expression was significantly lower on monocytes and T lymphocytes in periodontitis patients compared with healthy individuals (p < 0.05). Conclusions Periodontitis is associated with a distinct peripheral immune profile, characterized by reduced CD11b expression on monocytes and T lymphocytes and increased NK and NKT cell frequencies. This reduction in CD11b suggests a possible impairment of leukocyte adhesion-related immune mechanisms, which warrants further functional investigation.

Art therapy sebagai pendekatan kreatif dalam konseling untuk mengurangi kecemasan
abstractText: Kecemasan pada remaja merupakan masalah kesehatan mental yang kompleks, dipicu oleh faktor akademik, sosial, dan lingkungan, memerlukan intervensi efektif seperti art therapy. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkaji efektivitas art therapy dalam mengurangi kecemasan remaja melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan menganalisis studi terbitan lima tahun terakhir dari database seperti Google Scholar. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa art therapy (melalui lukis, musik, atau tari) signifikan menurunkan kecemasan, terutama pada remaja dengan Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) dan tekanan akademik, serta kelompok rentan seperti pasien kanker dan lansia. Efektivitasnya bervariasi tergantung durasi intervensi, metode, dan dukungan lingkungan. Simpulan penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa art therapy merupakan pendekatan terapeutik yang menjanjikan untuk mengelola kecemasan remaja, meski diperlukan adaptasi metode sesuai kebutuhan individu.

title: Socio-Technical Conflict and Adaptive Governance: Applying Agent-Based Modelling to Inter-Civilizational and Environmental Scenarios
abstractText: The paper is a thorough examination of socio-technical conflict and adaptive governance using agent-based modelling (ABM) that combines the computational simulation with the theory of systems and inter-civilizational literature. The research is inspired by the human-alien conflict analogy and uses analytical frameworks of heterogeneous agentsGEs of technologically and culturally distinct communities to support the impact of the combination of trust, information asymmetry, and adaptive policy patterns on the stability of the system and collaborative strengths. All emergent processes, including the formation of alliances, the process of policy adjustment, and conflict intensification, can be quantitatively studied in the proposed ABM framework where interactions vary in transparency, fidelity in communication, and flexibility on governance. Findings indicate that open information-exchange and evolving feedback systems are very effective in promoting trust and low entropy systemic states, which is typically achieved at equilibrium even in highly uncertain circumstances. On the other hand, there is cyclical instability and a possible breakdown of systems that are characterised by information opacy and stasis governance. The results highlight the importance of the structure of adaptive governance that is based on iterative learning, distributed decision-making, and real-time policy development that is vital to balance both in inter-civilizational and socio-ecological spheres. In addition to the astrobiological analogy, this research offers a conceptual and computational context on the reconsideration of governance in an epoch of mounting technological destabilization, environmental delicacy and world interdependence. The study provides a transdisciplinary template of designing next generations of governance systems that can sustain cooperation, reduce conflict, as well as create systemic stability across technological, ecological, and cultural boundaries because it reveals that the issue of resilience is not based on control, but rather on adaptatory coherence of agents.

title: Climate-Based Modeling of Invasive Species Impact on Urban Green Infrastructure Using CLIMEX and Remote Sensing Data
abstractText: The pace at which invasive alien species are established and spread is becoming a threat, especially to urban ecosystems, due, in part, to the variability of climates, urban growth, and fragmentation of habitats. These biological invasions are highly dangerous to urban green infrastructure (UGI), which sabotages biodiversity, ecological services, and ecological resilience in the long term. A unravelled modelling approach to employ the CLIMEX model of species distribution as well as the spatial analysis of ecosystems via remote sensing to observe invasion risk zones and map them in the fast urbanising landscapes was created in this work. The climatic suitability of chosen invasive species in the current and future climate conditions under parameters serving as temperature, precipitation, and humidity was simulated with the help of the CLIMEX model, and the land cover dynamics and vegetation indices (as well as the urban heat islands) were measured with the assistance of remote sensing data (Sentinel-2 and ModiS) measurements. It was possible to integrate these datasets using a GIS based multi-criteria methodology to create an Invasion Risk Index (IRI) to predict ecologically sensitive regions. The findings indicated that areas with an average rainfall, increasing temperatures, and discontinuous vegetation shows high ecological suitability of the invasive species, and this would be more so at the urban fringes, transport corridors, and industrial areas. These findings underscore the synergistic role of climatic and anthropogenic factors in shaping invasion dynamics and highlight the necessity for adaptive urban planning that incorporates ecological modeling outputs. The proposed framework offers a robust, scalable approach for predicting biological invasions, guiding urban biodiversity conservation strategies, and supporting policymakers in developing climate-resilient, biodiversity-secure urban ecosystems.

title: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
abstractText: Abstract Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

title: ‘One shunt fits all?’: a comparative laboratory study of antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters with retrospective clinical correlation
abstractText: Abstract Introduction Several antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters are commercially available, but direct comparative data on their biochemical and physical characteristics remain limited. Previous observations from our single-centre neurosurgical unit suggested that nominally similar catheter types may be associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain. We therefore conducted a prospective comparative study to investigate potential biochemical and physical differences between commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters. Methods Ares ® , Bactiseal ® and XABO ® catheters were compared for antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation products, elution characteristics and antimicrobial activity. Antibiotic elution was assessed during continuous saline perfusion at 20 mL/h and 37 °C over 8 weeks, while antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis was evaluated over 60 days. Catheter dimensions, elastic modulus and surface morphology were assessed using three-dimensional computed tomography, nanoindentation and scanning electron microscopy, respectively. An exploratory retrospective quality-improvement dataset from our single-centre unit was additionally analysed to compare the frequency of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain between catheter types. Results The three catheter systems showed product-specific differences in antibiotic content, rifampicin degradation profiles, elution characteristics, antimicrobial activity, dimensions, mechanical properties and surface morphology. XABO ® most closely matched the declared antibiotic concentrations and retained the greatest proportion of intact rifampicin, while Ares ® demonstrated the highest sustained clindamycin elution. All three catheters retained measurable activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis for 60 days, with XABO ® showing the largest numerical inhibition zones throughout. In the 395-patient retrospective clinical analysis, otherwise unexplained abdominal pain was recorded in 90/182 patients with Ares ® catheters (49.5%) compared with 12/108 patients with Bactiseal ® catheters (11.1%). After adjustment for age, sex, primary diagnosis, modified Rankin Scale score and activity level, Ares ® remained associated with greater odds of abdominal pain than Bactiseal ® (adjusted OR 6.89, 95% CI 2.58–18.43; p < 0.001). Conclusion Commercially available antibiotic-impregnated shunt catheters showed product-specific biochemical and physical variation, while catheter type was associated with different rates of otherwise unexplained abdominal pain in a retrospective single-centre analysis. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality or clinical superiority. Prospective multicentre studies are required to determine whether catheter-specific properties translate into clinically meaningful differences and should influence individualised shunt selection.

title: Efektivitas Model Discovery Learning dalam Meningkatkan Pemahaman Konsep IPAS Siswa Kelas V SD
abstractText: Conceptual understanding is a central goal of integrated natural and social science (IPAS) instruction in primary schools, yet it is hard to achieve when pupils only listen to explanations. This article reviews the effectiveness of discovery learning in improving fifth-grade pupils' understanding of IPAS concepts. A library research method was applied to books and journal articles published between 2000 and 2015. The review indicates that discovery learning allows pupils to construct concepts through observation, data collection, and drawing their own conclusions. However, its advantage appears only when discovery is guided by the teacher; unguided discovery has not been shown to outperform direct instruction, particularly for novice learners. Guided discovery learning is therefore worth considering for IPAS lessons in grade five, provided that teachers prepare problems, materials, and guiding questions carefully.

title: Low-Weber-Number Droplet Splitting and Retention on Circular Hydrophilic Patterns Embedded in a Superhydrophobic Surface
abstractText: Abstract Localized wettability patterning provides a passive strategy for regulating droplet impact, rebound, and retention without external energy input. In this study, the impact dynamics of deionized-water droplets on circular hydrophilic patterns embedded in a superhydrophobic surface were experimentally investigated using high-speed imaging. The Weber number (We = ρdv2/σ, representing the ratio of inertial force to surface-tension force) was varied from 2 to 150, and three dimensionless hydrophilic-pattern diameters, D* = 0.4, 0.8, and 1.2, were considered. The results show that the hydrophilic pattern has a limited influence on the early inertia-dominated spreading stage but plays a decisive role during recoiling and rebound through contact-line pinning. Depending on We and D*, three characteristic impact regimes are identified: adhesion, partial rebound, and splashing. Notably, for a circular hydrophilic pattern with a diameter of 1 mm (D* = 0.4), partial rebound occurs at We = 3.5. During partial rebound, the lower portion of the droplet remains pinned within the hydrophilic region, whereas the upper portion detaches through liquid-bridge breakup, enabling passive generation of secondary droplets. The normalized retained volume V* increases markedly with D* but exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence on We, reflecting the competition between enhanced pinning and inertia-driven fragmentation. An empirical correlation, V* = a0+a1D* + a2We + a3(D*)2 + a4D*We + cWe2, is proposed to quantify the retained liquid volume within the partial-rebound regime. Contact-line analysis further reveals that the maximum outer-rim diameter and the maximum three-phase contact-line diameter both increase approximately linearly with We, whereas the difference between them gradually decreases as inertia increases. These findings provide quantitative guidance for passive droplet capture, controllable generation of millimeter- and submillimeter-scale droplets, and the design of wettability-patterned surfaces for microfluidic and thermal-management applications.

title: Upaya Pencegahan Sebagai Bentuk Pengendalian Perilaku Menyimpang Anak Melalui Pembinaan Karakter dan Pemberdayaan di Griya Abhipraya Tanon
abstractText: Artikel ini mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan program pembinaan karakter dan pemberdayaan bagi anak yang mengikuti pembinaan di Griya Abhipraya Tanon, Kabupaten Sragen. Program dikembangkan sebagai upaya pencegahan untuk mendukung pengendalian perilaku menyimpang sekaligus memperkuat kesadaran diri, karakter positif, motivasi perubahan, keterampilan praktis, dan kesiapan reintegrasi sosial. Artikel menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif berbasis pelaksanaan kegiatan Kuliah Kerja Nyata. Data diperoleh melalui observasi awal, koordinasi dengan pemangku kepentingan, asesmen sosial, perencanaan program, observasi selama intervensi, diskusi kelompok, tanya jawab, dan evaluasi kegiatan. Intervensi dilaksanakan melalui materi motivasi, pembinaan karakter, refleksi diri, perencanaan masa depan, dan pelatihan keterampilan praktis. Program menggunakan landasan Teori Sistem Ekologi Bronfenbrenner, Teori Perkembangan Psikososial Erik Erikson, Teori Belajar Sosial Albert Bandura, dan pendekatan Motivational Interviewing. Pelaksanaan kegiatan menunjukkan partisipasi aktif dan respons positif peserta. Peserta dilaporkan memperoleh pemahaman yang lebih baik mengenai konsekuensi perilaku masa lalu, nilai-nilai karakter positif, motivasi untuk memperbaiki diri, harapan dan rencana masa depan, serta pengalaman keterampilan praktis. Temuan tersebut merupakan gambaran hasil kegiatan dan tidak dimaksudkan sebagai bukti efektivitas kausal jangka panjang. Program menunjukkan pentingnya integrasi pengembangan individu, dukungan lingkungan, pendekatan komunikasi, dan keterampilan produktif dalam pembimbingan kemasyarakatan yang bersifat preventif bagi anak.

title: Rational Design of a Cytochrome P450 for Efficient 11α-Hydroxylation of Steroids by Integrating Genome Mining and Global Dynamic Simulations
abstractText: Abstract The 11α-hydroxylation of steroids is essential for their semisynthesis. However, natural 11α-hydroxylases are scarce and generally exhibit low catalytic activity. In this study, a structure–function-guided computational approach was applied to identify a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CosaP450) with 11α-hydroxylation activity. By modulating the flexibility of the gating helix (N62-E75), the engineered variant MT3 (T72Q/F70T/Y226Q) increased the production of 11α,17α-hydroxyprogesterone (11α,17α-OHP) from 680 mg/L to 1140 mg/L. Then, the targeted engineering of the substrate channel and active site was employed based on the multiscale MD simulations, and the mutant MT6 (T72Q/F70T/Y226Q/V374A/G137T/E118G) achieved a yield of 1863 mg/L. MD analysis revealed that V374A relieved channel steric hindrance, while G137T/E118G remodeled the hydrogen-bond network to stabilize the binding conformation. Redox partner engineering further enhanced the titer of MT6 AnCPR to 2489 mg/L. This work establishes a computational framework for rational discovery and engineering of efficient 11α-hydroxylases, providing a promising strategy for enzymatic steroid functionalization.

title: Everyday Instagram behavior maps distinct facets of loneliness in young adults
abstractText: Abstract Loneliness is a major health risk and is often hard to detect. It is multidimensional and can involve social, emotional, and structural facets with different causes and behavioral consequences. An open question is whether these facets can be differentiated in everyday Instagram behavior. We analyzed consented Instagram data exports from 415 US college students and modeled five validated measures related to loneliness using activity patterns, language, and images. Multimodal traces distinguished subjective loneliness but were less informative for structural isolation. Model explanation analyses revealed dissociable signatures: social loneliness was linked to low interpersonal engagement (fewer likes and comments), whereas emotional loneliness was linked to negative affect (negative language and sad/angry facial expressions) and late-night activity. Together, these results provide a cross-measure behavioral “construct map” of loneliness, suggesting that multimodal digital traces can separate markers of dissatisfaction with social connections from markers of emotional isolation, moving beyond generic prediction toward construct-sensitive characterization. Because the sample was of college age, predominantly female, and largely Asian or White, an important next step is to test whether these signatures generalize to more diverse populations.

title: Becoming a Published Scholar: Indonesian EFL Teacher Educators Negotiating Feedback, Identity, and Recognition
abstractText: While existing research often highlights the struggles of early-career academics, less attention is paid to how experienced scholars in peripheral contexts navigate the peer review process. This study explores the challenges Indonesian EFL faculty face when responding to reviewer feedback and the strategies they use to navigate these challenges. Guided by academic literacy theory, the study employed a qualitative case study with three female teacher educators and one male teacher educator from four different Indonesian universities. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings reveal two key insights: (1) participants faced persistent challenges spanning temporal, epistemic, social, and institutional dimensions including difficulty balancing revision with competing academic, familial, and doctoral responsibilities, impediments in interpreting ambiguous reviewer feedback, limited collegial collaboration, restricted access to quality references, inadequate publication funding, and infrequent professional development opportunities; and (2) they employed a diverse repertoire of adaptive strategies encompassing self-regulation and task prioritization, peer consultation, cultivation of supportive research environments, mobilization of alternative resources, pursuit of available funding and rewards, and engagement with external mentoring and training programs reflecting a determined scholarly agency that largely compensated for the insufficiencies of formal institutional support. These findings challenge individualistic accounts of academic publishing and highlight the importance of recognizing the structural and contextual conditions that shape scholarly participation in the Global South. The study concludes that more equitable academic infrastructures, sustained mentoring, accessible professional development, and institutional support are needed to enable Indonesian EFL teacher educators and other scholars in peripheral contexts to participate more confidently and sustainably in international knowledge production. Biodegradation and Photodegradation of Mg, Ca, Zn, and Cu Complexes of Biodegradable Chelating Agents (EDDS, HIDS, MGDA, and GLDA)
abstractText: Abstract The environmental fate of biodegradable aminopolycarboxylate chelating agents is strongly influenced by metal complexation; however, the combined effects of central metal ions and ligand structure on degradation behavior remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the biodegradation and photodegradation of the Mg, Ca, Zn, and Cu complexes of four biodegradable chelating agents (EDDS, HIDS, MGDA, and GLDA) were investigated under activated sludge and UV-lamp irradiation conditions. Biodegradation tests revealed metal-dependent behavior: complexes with the alkaline earth metals Mg and Ca were readily degraded, whereas complexes with the transition metals Zn and Cu, except for the EDDS complexes, exhibited high persistence. A qualitative inverse relationship was observed between biodegradability and metal–ligand stability. In contrast, photodegradation exhibited a distinct metal-specific pattern: Cu complexes underwent photodegradation, whereas Mg, Ca, and Zn complexes showed limited photodegradation regardless of ligand identity. These results demonstrate that the degradability of metal–chelate complexes cannot be predicted solely from the behavior of the corresponding free ligands and highlight the importance of considering metal complexation when evaluating the environmental persistence of biodegradable chelating agents in metal-containing aquatic systems.

Tribological Behavior of Ti-6Al-4V Alloys Processed by Selective Laser Melting and Conventional Casting Process
abstractText: This work presents a detailed assessment of the microstructural features and tribological behaviour of Ti6Al4V alloy produced by conventional casting followed by rolling (CR) and selective laser melting (SLM). The two fabrication routes yield markedly different microstructures: the CR alloy develops a dualphase α + β microstructure, whereas the SLM alloy forms a fine martensitic α′ lath morphology with enhanced hardness. Tribological experiments performed under various loads and sliding speeds reveal clear distinctions in frictional response and wear characteristics. The CR samples exhibit deeper ploughing grooves, stronger oxidation effects, and higher coefficients of friction, indicating that abrasive and oxidationassisted wear dominate their surface degradation. In contrast, the SLM samples show shallower wear tracks, reduced friction, and improved resistance to material removal, with delamination and adhesive wear occurring only under more severe test conditions. The lower COF and diminished wear severity observed in the SLM alloy highlight the advantages of its refined microstructure in stabilizing interfacial contact and reducing frictional energy losses. Overall, the results confirm the superior tribological performance of SLMprocessed Ti6Al4V for applications demanding high wear resistance and structural reliability.

title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
abstractText: Abstract The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal–insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current–voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

title: Evaluating the Geometric Brownian Motion Model for Gold Price Movements (XAU/USD) across Market Conditions
abstractText: This study evaluates the performance of the Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) model in predicting prices and estimating the risk of XAU/USD under stable and unstable economic conditions. Daily closing price data are divided into in-sample and out-of-sample periods, where return and volatility parameters are estimated from the in-sample data and applied in Monte Carlo simulations. Prediction accuracy is assessed using the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), while risk is measured using Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES). The results indicate that MAPE values exceed 20% in both economic conditions, suggesting that the predictive accuracy of the GBM model remains moderate. Although the model performs slightly better during stable periods, the difference is not statistically significant. In contrast, risk estimation results show that VaR and ES range between 58% and 59%, with higher values observed during unstable periods. This reflects an increase in market risk driven by higher volatility. Overall, the findings suggest that while GBM is capable of capturing the general movement of gold prices, it has limitations in accurately predicting price levels and capturing extreme market fluctuations, particularly during periods of economic instability.

title: Interactive Digital Media-Assisted SSCS Learning: A Solution to Enhance Problem-Solving Ability and Alleviate Mathematics Anxiety
abstractText: Problem-solving is a practical skill that students must master in 21st-century learning. However, various findings indicate that this capability remains low among junior high school students, who are beginning to study mathematical concepts in greater depth. Anxiety toward the subject matter, teachers, and mathematics instruction itself is a key factor influencing students' mathematical problem-solving performance. To address this, this study aims to examine the effect of the Search, Solve, Create, and Share (SSCS) learning model, a model that provides a clear roadmap for students to implement Polya's problem-solving steps, assisted by interactive digital media (PhET and Mathigon), on students' problem-solving ability and anxiety. This quasi-experimental study used a factorial design and included eighth-grade students. The research sample was selected using the cluster random sampling technique. Data were collected using a test instrument and a mathematics anxiety questionnaire and were subsequently analyzed using a two-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results of the study indicate that: (1) Hypothesis testing showed that there was a significant effect of different learning models on students’ problem-solving ability, with Fobs (= 8.405) > Ftab (= 4.016). Furthermore, based on the marginal means, the interactive digital media PhET-assisted SSCS model was more effective, with a mean score of 66.129, than PBL, which had a mean score of 56.222. (2) Students with lower levels of anxiety demonstrate better problem-solving performance, as indicated by the marginal means, with low anxiety (=72.822) > moderate anxiety (= 61.905) > high anxiety (= 52.833); and (3) there is no interaction effect between the learning models and anxiety levels. These findings suggest that integrating SSCS syntax with the visualization features in PhET and Mathigon provides effective scaffolding that reduces cognitive load, thereby improving learning outcomes across all levels of student anxiety..Keywords: SSCS model, interactive digital media, problem solving ability, mathematical anxiety, phet and mathigon.

Mental health of migrants in South Asia: a scoping review
abstractText: Purpose Migration in South Asia is shaped by diverse drivers such as economic needs, conflict, persecution, natural disasters and sociocultural factors. Migrants across typologies are vulnerable to mental health challenges. However, research in this domain remains fragmented. This scoping review aims to synthesize existing literature on migrant mental health in South Asia and map key trends, identify research gaps and draw implications for future research, policy and practice. Design/methodology/approach A systematic search of peer-reviewed literature was conducted across databases including Scopus, Web of Science and PsycINFO. Studies using both qualitative and quantitative methods were included. Data extraction and thematic synthesis was conducted to analyse study characteristics, research methodologies, mental health outcomes and associated risk and protective factors. Findings Eighty studies met the inclusion criteria, with nearly half published since 2020. Most were cross-sectional and concentrated in India, Bangladesh and Nepal. Commonly studied mental health issues included depression, anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder – particularly among refugees, internally displaced persons and labour migrants. Risk factors included violence and trauma, economic hardship, social isolation and perceived discrimination; while protective factors such as family support, cultural practices and community resilience were highlighted, though resilience was often conceptualised narrowly as an individual trait. Research on queer and transgender migrants, children, older adults and help-seeking behaviours was notably absent. Originality/value This review underscores that while the burden of poor mental health among migrants in South Asia is significant, research priorities vary based on the migrant typology. Significant research gaps persist, including limited longitudinal studies and participatory research methods. Pathways to migrant mental health and wellbeing and intersectional analyses of mental health precarity are also unexplored. Future work should consider dimensions of precarity among migrants in the region to better understand mental health vulnerabilities.

Navigating resilience and barriers in mental health care: retrospective accounts of ethnic minority older adults during the COVID-19 pandemic in remote Northern Thailand
abstractText: Abstract Background Ethnic minority older adults living in remote mountainous areas may face substantial barriers to accessing mental health care, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, limited evidence exists regarding their experiences of mental health care and the factors influencing service utilization in these underserved communities. This study explored the retrospectively recalled experiences of ethnic minority older adults and their caregivers in navigating mental health care during the COVID-19 pandemic and the continuing consequences of these experiences in remote Northern Thailand. Methods A qualitative study design was used. Face-to-face, in-depth interviews were conducted with 22 participants, including 11 ethnic minority older adults with mental health problems and 11 family caregivers. Although interviews were conducted between January and March 2024, participants were asked to retrospectively describe their experiences with mental health care during the COVID-19 pandemic and any continuing consequences in the post-pandemic period. Data were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Results Two overarching themes and eleven sub-themes were identified. The first theme, Challenges in providing mental health care for ethnic minority older adults with mental health problems , described barriers related to limited mental health literacy, restricted access to mental health services and technology, geographic isolation, perceived disparities in service provision, inadequate caregiver preparedness, and the psychological consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic. The second theme, Perceptions and expectations of mental health care , reflected the importance of culturally responsive care, cultural and spiritual practices, family support, alternative approaches to care, and strategies for improving mental health service delivery. Participants also described resilience through family relationships, community engagement, and cultural resources that supported coping during the pandemic. Conclusions Ethnic minority older adults in remote communities retrospectively described multiple barriers to accessing and utilizing mental health services during the COVID-19 pandemic. At the same time, family support, community participation, and cultural and spiritual practices were perceived as important resources for coping with mental health challenges. These findings suggest the importance of culturally responsive and accessible mental health services that are aligned with the needs and contexts of ethnic minority communities.

title: A General Platform for the Construction of Sulfonylated Heterocycles with Indoles as Catalysts via Visible-Light Photocatalysis
abstractText: Abstract A general photocatalytic platform has been developed for the synthesis of sulfonyl-substituted heterocycles from alkenes/alkynes and alkyl sulfonyl chlorides by using indoles as catalysts. This platform relies on the radical cascade cyclization without metal and base involvement and can be carried out with water as the reaction solvent. Mechanistic studies have indicated that the in situ-generated indole oligomers are the photocatalysts for this reaction.

title: La influencia de las redes sociales en los casos de violencia juvenil: una aproximación criminológica desde la teoría de la imitación de Gabriel Tarde y la asociación diferencial de Edwin H. Sutherland
abstractText: In recent years, digital technologies have transformed the ways young people interact, as they find social media to be new spaces for communication, identity construction, the development of a sense of belonging, and group integration. However, these same digital spaces can also facilitate the expansion of various expressions of youth violence, such as cyberbullying, the spread of violent content, symbolic violence, the promotion of aggressive behaviors, and the reproduction of discriminatory discourses. The objective of this work is to analyze the influence of social media on manifestations of youth violence from a criminological perspective. To this end, a narrative literature review of scientific work on digital violence, social learning, and youth behavior was conducted as part of a qualitative documentary research project. This review links the selected studies to two classic criminological theories: the theory of imitation developed by Gabriel Tarde and the theory of differential association proposed by Edwin H. Sutherland, aiming to understand how their approaches contribute to interpreting these manifestations of violence in digital environments.

title: Confinement-Induced Suppression of Vapor Pressure in Hydrocarbons: Elevated-Pressure DSC Measurements and Molecular Simulation
abstractText: Abstract Phase behavior of hydrocarbons in nanosized porous media is important for understanding fluid behavior in confined environments, yet direct experimental validation under elevated-pressure conditions remains limited. In this work, elevated-pressure differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) was used to measure boiling points of n-heptane and toluene confined in well-defined mesoporous silica materials (SBA-15 and SBA-16) at pressures up to 1300 kPa. The experimentally derived vapor pressure curves show a systematic suppression relative to bulk fluids across all pressures. Kelvin equation predictions and Gibbs Ensemble Monte Carlo (GEMC) simulations provide thermodynamic and qualitative molecular-level support for the observed confinement-induced phase behavior. In contrast, shale samples with low pore volumes and broader, more heterogeneous pore structures did not show a distinct confinement peak under the present experimental conditions. These findings provide elevated-pressure experimental data for confinement-induced phase behavior in well-defined mesoporous model systems and offer a benchmark for comparison with thermodynamic models and molecular simulations.

Practical considerations for epigenetic editing experiments and clinical applications
abstractText: Abstract Background The discovery that CRISPR can be repurposed for targeted regulation of gene expression without inducing double-stranded breaks has paved the way for CRISPR-based epigenetic editing. Compared to other editing methods such as ZFPs and TALEs, CRISPR has the advantage of low cost, simplicity and multiplexing ability. Great strides have been made towards the clinical translation of these tools, and many recent studies have demonstrated long-lasting epigenetic changes in vivo, increasing the potential for therapeutically relevant outcomes. Main body On Addgene, there are currently > 700 different CRISPR-dCas9 tools available for CRISPR activation (CRISPRa), CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) and CRISPR-dCas9 epigenetics. Whilst this provides a broad range of tools to choose from, there is little consensus on which to use, when to use them, the cell types they are most suitable for, and how different epigenetic effectors interact with one another. Moreover, it is unclear how the existing epigenomic and transcriptomic contexts affect durability, efficiency and specificity of editing, raising further uncertainties about experimental design. Several unresolved questions remain: how many guides and effectors are required, what level of epigenetic change is required to exert functional outputs, and how does editing interact with other aspects of epigenetic and transcriptional machinery? Conclusions Our understanding of how epigenetic crosstalk contributes to epigenetic editing efficiency and how this informs experimental design is lagging. This review aims to highlight successes and challenges within the epigenetic editing field both in vitro and in vivo, providing a molecular framework of considerations for designing an editing experiment, focusing on the use of dCas9-based tools.

title: Revealing Redox Regulatory Pathways Governing Tardigrade Osmobiosis
abstractText: Abstract Able to survive dehydration through anydrobiosis, freezing temperature through cryobiosis, and extreme osmotic pressure through osmobiosis, tardigrades, otherwise known as waterbears, are valuable organisms to study organismal stress response. However, the signaling pathways involved in their survival are still being uncovered. Herein, we investigate the cysteine-mediated redox regulatory pathways involved in tardigrade osmobiosis induction. We first quantify the reactivity of the tardigrade cysteinome through Quantitative Thiol Reactivity Profiling and reveal for proteins involved in signal transduction pathways to have hyperreactive cysteines. We then quantify cysteine oxidative changes via proteomics during osmobiote formation induced by NaCl and sucrose and uncover that polyamines play a regulatory role during osmobiote formation. An increase in the polyamine spermidine during osmobiosis implicates it as a key player during osmobiosis. Further analysis of the proteins becoming oxidized during osmobiosis reveal that phosphorylation-based signaling from a protein phosphatase 2A-like protein and extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 has a modulatory effect on the induction into and recovery from osmobiosis. In sum, our work is the first to quantify and characterize the tardigrade cysteinome, determine its redox regulation in osmobiosis, and validate its downstream collateral effects during osmobiote formation.

When expertise fails: detection of artificial intelligence - generated vitiligo imagery across the spectrum of dermatological experience; a cross-sectional exploratory study
abstractText: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (AI) can produce highly realistic dermatological images, raising concerns about clinicians’ ability to distinguish authentic pathology from synthetic representations. To assess whether dermatological expertise influences the detection of AI-generated vitiligo images, and to evaluate the self-detection capabilities of the algorithm, we conducted a participant-blinded cross-sectional study in which 31 dermatologists, stratified by experience, classified one AI-generated vitiligo image alongside three real controls while blinded to the number and identity of the synthetic images. Interrater agreement was assessed using Fleiss’ kappa statistic, and the synthetic image was additionally evaluated using three large multimodal models. Residents detected the AI-generated image more frequently than senior dermatologists and key opinion leaders. After disclosure of the correct classifications, the experts identified specific biological inconsistencies, whereas residents relied primarily on intuitive impressions, and the performance of the AI models varied across the detection and post-disclosure artifact-recognition tasks. This study is limited by its evaluation of a single AI-generated image depicting a single disease (vitiligo), and the findings may therefore not be generalizable to other dermatological morphologies, image-generation prompts, or multi-image scenarios. In this exploratory study, greater clinical experience was associated with reduced detection of the evaluated synthetic image; whether this reflects a general effect of expertise requires further study. These findings highlight the emerging risks associated with medical AI and support the integration of AI-focused visual analysis into dermatology education.
