Surgical versus non-surgical management of pediatric medial epicondyle fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background The optimal management of medial epicondyle fractures remains controversial, particularly in displaced fracture without incarceration. Traditionally, non-surgical treatment remains the treatment of choice for the management of medial epicondyle fracture; however recent evidence suggesting favorable outcomes with surgical fixation has increased interest in operative management. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare surgical versus non-surgical treatment for the management of medial epicondyle fracture in pediatric population to determine the optimal management therapy. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar and Clinical trial govt. was conducted from inception to April 2026 according to PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261393871 ) . Randomized controlled trials and observational studies were included. Statistical analyses were performed using a random-effects model in RevMan 5.4. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool and Newcastle–Ottawa Scale, while certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Results Six comparative studies involving 564 pediatric patients were included, comprising two randomized controlled trials and four cohort studies. Surgical fixation significantly reduced the risk of non-union (RR = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.02–0.39; p = 0.001) and worse cosmetic VAS scores (MD = − 8.56, 95% CI: −12.66 to − 4.46; p < 0.0001), favoring non-surgical management. However, surgery was associated with a significantly greater likelihood of requiring additional surgery (RR = 13.37, 95% CI: 5.20–34.35; p < 0.00001). No significant differences were observed between groups for DASH scores, elbow flexion or extension deficits, PedsQL scores, or valgus instability tests. Conclusion Surgical treatment reduces nonunion but is associated with worse cosmetic outcomes in pediatric medial epicondyle fracture. However, its effect on functional outcomes remains uncertain compared with non-surgical treatment. Treatment decisions should therefore be individualized based on clinical and patient-specific factors.

title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids
abstractText: Abstract Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as “Mussel Watch”.

Furthermore, pNZ removal in water was applied to SPPS of ε-Lys-branched peptides and hybrid pNZ/Fmoc SPPS. title: Cinnamon Polysaccharide Regulates FUNDC1-Dependent Mitochondrial Autophagy to Reduce Oxidative Stress-Driven Mammary Gland Aging in Dairy Cows
abstractText: Abstract Mastitis causes oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired lactation in dairy cows. This study investigated whether FUNDC1 (FUN14 domain-containing protein 1)-associated mitochondrial quality control protects mammary tissue from oxidative stress-driven senescence and whether cinnamon polysaccharide (CP) can restore this pathway during mastitis recovery. Mastitis-associated oxidative stress reduced FUNDC1 expression, disrupted mitochondrial dynamics by suppressing fusion and promoting fission, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and increased senescence markers in bovine mammary epithelial cells. FUNDC1 overexpression alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction and senescence-associated changes. Mechanistically, the E3 ubiquitin ligase FANCL contributed to the proteasome-dependent reduction of FUNDC1 under oxidative stress. CP treatment restored FUNDC1 expression, reduced inflammation and oxidative stress, improved mitochondrial homeostasis, and enhanced postmastitis milk-yield recovery when combined with antibiotic treatment. These findings identify the FANCL–FUNDC1 axis as a link between oxidative stress and mammary gland senescence and support CP as a functional adjunct for mastitis management.

abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan menggambarkan pelaksanaan pembelajaran menulis teks prosedur dengan model experiential learning berbantuan praktik hastakarya, keterampilan menulis teks prosedur setelah pembelajaran serta faktor pendukung dan penghambat pelaksanaannya. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian dan uraian tersebut dapat disimpulkan pelaksanaan pembelajaran menulis teks prosedur dengan model experiential learning berbantuan praktik hastakrya pada siswa kelas V berlangsung melalui 4 tahap : Siswa membuat hastakarya dirumah sebagai pengalaman konkret, mencatat peoses secara berurutaan sebagai bentuk pengamatan, kemudian menyusun teks prosedur pada LKPD sesuai struktur yang telah ditetapkan. title: Determinants of Delayed Antenatal Care Initiation among Low-Income Families in Indonesia
abstractText: Objective: Ensuring proper and timely antenatal care (ANC) can reduce poor birth outcomes among low-income families. This study examined the determinants of delayed ANC initiation among low-income families in Indonesia. Material and Methods: The study examined 25,073 women. We used delayed ANC initiation as a dependent variable and eight independent variables: residence, age, marital status, education, employment, parity, insurance, and wealth. In the last step, the research employed binary logistic regression.Results: 26.4% of women among low-income families delayed ANC initiation. Women in rural areas were 1.091 times more likely than those in urban areas to delay ANC initiation (95% CI 1.087-1.096). All age groups were less likely to delay ANC initiation than those aged ≤ 19. Divorced/widowed women were 1.390 times more likely than those married to delay ANC initiation (95% CI 1.373-1.407). Women at all education levels were more likely to delay ANC initiation than women with a college education. Employed women were 1.030 times more likely than unemployed women to delay ANC initiation (95% CI 1.026-1.034). The poorest were 1.538 times more likely to delay ANC initiation than the poorer (95% CI 1.532-1.544). Women with any insurance type were less likely than those without insurance to delay ANC initiation. Women with all parity types were more likely than primiparous women to delay ANC initiation.Conclusion: Delayed ANC initiation among low-income families in Indonesia is driven by multiple socioeconomic and structural factors. Targeted and context-specific policies are needed to improve early ANC uptake.

Reordering of Retinal Reactions Underlies Reversal of Proton-Pump Directionality
abstractText: Abstract Light-driven proton-pumping rhodopsins transport protons either outward or inward across membranes, but the molecular determinants of transport vectoriality remain unclear. An outward proton-pumping rhodopsin from Pseudomonas putida (PspR) was previously converted into an inward pump by substituting only three amino acid residues. Here, time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy reveals that wild-type PspR accepts a proton with a 13-cis retinal chromophore, whereas the engineered inward-pumping PspR triple mutant accepts a proton with an all-trans chromophore, as observed in schizorhodopsins. Intermediate mutant analysis shows that D73F/T78C generates an all-trans M intermediate, while previous transport measurements showed that adding T77S further enhances inward-pumping activity. These findings link reversal of proton-pump vectoriality to reordering of retinal reisomerization and Schiff-base reprotonation, suggesting a strategy for engineering transport directionality in microbial rhodopsins.

title: Pengaruh Daya Tarik dan Interaksi Parasosial Virtual Influencer Arbie Seo terhadap Minat Beli Produk Richeese Factory di Kalangan Gen Z Kota Semarang
abstractText: The growth of social media has encouraged the use of virtual influencers as part of digital marketing communication strategies. One such virtual influencer, Arbie SEO, serves as a brand ambassador for Richeese Factory. This study aims to examine the influence of the attractiveness and parasocial interaction of the virtual influencer Arbie SEO on the purchase intention for Richeese Factory products among Generation Z in Semarang City, both partially and simultaneously. The study employs a quantitative, explanatory approach. The sample consists of 100 Generation Z respondents in Semarang City, selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected via a questionnaire using a Likert scale and analyzed through multiple linear regression. The results indicate that the attractiveness of the virtual influencer Arbie SEO has a positive and significant effect on purchase intention, with a t-value of 4.308 and a significance level of 0.000. Conversely, parasocial interaction does not have a significant effect on purchase intention, with a t-value of 1.277 and a significance level of 0.205. Simultaneously, both attractiveness and parasocial interaction have a significant effect on purchase intention, with an F-value of 73.265 and a significance level of 0.000. An R-squared value of 0.602 indicates that these two variables account for 60.2% of the variation in purchase intention, while the remaining 39.8% is explained by factors outside the scope of this study. The Theory of Planned Behavior remains relevant as a grand theory for providing the conceptual framework for this research.

title: Genomic analysis of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with a severe episode of self-trauma and urinary tract infection
abstractText: Abstract Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales are emerging pathogens of major importance in veterinary medicine. This study describes the clinical, microbiological, and genomic characteristics of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from a dog with paraparesis and concurrent pyelonephritis, chronic cystitis, and a self-traumatized limb lesion. A 12-year-old mixed-breed female dog underwent repeated antimicrobial therapy during hospitalization. Urine obtained by cystocentesis and wound samples were cultured, and ESBL-producing strains were characterized by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequence-based analysis. CTX-M-55-producing E. coli sequence type (ST) 457, phylogroup F, O11:H25, and fimH 145, was recovered from urine and wound samples, while the wound sample also yielded a CTX-M-15- and SHV-2-producing K. pneumoniae ST39, KL149:OL2α.2. The two closely related E. coli strains differed by 96 single nucleotide polymorphisms, despite sharing the same ST, resistome, plasmid replicons, and virulence profile. ESBL-positive strains carried multiple virulence genes, with the E. coli strains classified as extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli strains. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae ST39 in an animal in Brazil. The co-occurrence of ESBL-producing E. coli ST457 and K. pneumoniae ST39 in the same dog highlights the potential for companion animals to harbor clinically relevant multidrug-resistant lineages and reinforces the need for continuous antimicrobial resistance monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship in this sector.

abstractText: In the current era of rapid digital transformation and the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education, pre-service teachers are required not only to use information and communication technologies but also to apply AI in educational activities ethically, responsibly, and safely. This study aims to examine how pre-service teachers’ AI and digital ethics competence relates to their teaching competence and teaching interest. The study examined the statistical relationships among AI and digital ethics competence, teaching competence, and teaching interest among 311 pre-service teacher students. Data were collected using a five-point self-assessment questionnaire, and factor and regression analyses were conducted. The results revealed that AI and digital ethics competence was positively associated with both teaching interest and teaching competence, while teaching competence demonstrated a moderate positive relationship with teaching interest. These findings suggest that AI and digital ethics competence may support teaching interest both directly and indirectly through teaching competence. Based on these findings, the study recommends integrating AI, digital ethics, and responsible AI use into teacher education curricula in conjunction with professional pedagogical methods and practical teaching experiences.

title: Analysis of driver memory with V2X-enabled weighted speed in car-following traffic flow model
abstractText: In connected vehicle environments, drivers no longer rely solely on their own perception of the vehicle ahead, Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication now allows them to access real-time weighted speed information from surrounding traffic, while their car-following decisions are still influenced by recollection of past driving states, referred to here as driver memory. This study explores how these two factors, cognitive memory and V2X-based weighted speed awareness, jointly govern car-following dynamics by extending the classical Full Velocity Difference (FVD) model to include both effects explicitly. Through linear stability analysis, the stability criterion of the proposed model is derived and the results show that the combined inclusion of memory and weighted speed information enlarges the stable traffic flow region well beyond what is achieved by the conventional FVD model. Near the neutral stability boundary, a nonlinear analysis based on the reductive perturbation approach is used to derive the modified Korteweg–de Vries (mKdV) equation, whose kink–antikink soliton solution captures the density wave behavior that develops close to this critical threshold. The energy consumption is calculated to check how much memory and V2X information affect traffic disturbances. The simulation results agree with the analytical results, confirming that the proposed model exhibits markedly reduced stop-and-go oscillations and lower energy dissipation than earlier models.

A Practical Guide to a Solar-Powered Fruit Fly Trap for Developing Science Process Skills in Junior High School Students
abstractText: Background: Practical science learning requires contextual learning resources that connect scientific concepts with authentic phenomena and local problems. At the study site, a needs analysis indicated a need for a structured practical guide for renewable-energy learning. Aims: This study developed and evaluated a practical guide integrating a solar-powered fruit fly trap and examined changes in students’ science process skills (SPS) after implementation. Methods: The study used research and development with the ADDIE framework. The guide was developed, revised through expert validation, and implemented with 30 ninth-grade students at SMP Negeri 07 Seluma, Bengkulu, Indonesia. Data were collected through observation, teacher interview, a student-needs questionnaire, expert validation, a 25-item student-response questionnaire, and a 30-item SPS pretest–posttest.Results: The needs questionnaire yielded a mean of 77.30%, with 10 of 31 students (32.26%) indicating the guide was very needed and 21 (67.74%) indicating it was needed. Expert validation yielded 93% for material, 90% for media, 87% for language, and 89% for SPS, with an overall feasibility of 89.75%. The mean SPS score increased from 51.25 to 90.17, a 38.92-point increase, with a mean N-gain of 0.798 (high); all eight SPS indicators were in the high category. Student responses averaged 83.97%, with 28 students (93.55%) classified as very good and two (6.45%) as good. Conclusion: The guide was judged very feasible and well received, and its implementation was accompanied by substantial pre–post improvement in SPS. Because the study used a one-group pretest–posttest design without a control group, the results should be interpreted as evidence of pre–post improvement rather than definitive causal proof.

UNVEILING THE ROLE OF α-MnO2 NANORODS IN BOOSTING ELECTROCHEMICAL PERFORMANCE OF AC–MnO2 SYMMETRIC SUPERCAPACITORS
abstractText: Activated carbon (AC) - Manganese dioxide (MnO2) composite electrodes have attracted significant attention for supercapacitor applications due to the synergistic combination of electric double-layer capacitance from carbon materials and pseudocapacitive charge storage from MnO2. Despite their promising performance, the influence of MnO2 morphology on electrochemical behavior remains insufficiently understood when crystal phase and mass loading are controlled. In this work, α-MnO2 nanorods and α-MnO2 particles were synthesized via a hydrothermal method and incorporated into AC matrices with identical MnO2 mass loading to systematically evaluate the effect of morphology on charge-discharge performance. Structural characterization confirms that both materials possess the same α-phase, while distinct one-dimensional and particulate morphologies are observed. Electrochemical measurements show that the nanorod-based composite delivers a superior gravimetric capacitance of 40.67 F g-1 and a higher specific energy of 7.36 Wh kg-1 compared to the particle-based counterpart. These findings highlight morphology engineering of α-MnO2 as an effective strategy to further enhance the performance of AC–MnO2 composite electrodes for supercapacitors.

title: Exploring the Effectiveness of Values Integration in Social Studies on Students’ Empathy and Cooperation of Grade 4 Pupils in a Selected School in Lutayan District II
abstractText: Values integration in Social Studies is operationally defined as the deliberate incorporation of moral, civic, and social values into classroom instruction to develop students’ behavioral, emotional, and social competencies. This study examined the association between values integration in Social Studies and the empathy and cooperation of Grade 4 pupils in a selected public elementary school in Lutayan District II, Sultan Kudarat, Philippines, during School Year 2025–2026. A descriptive-correlational research design was employed, involving 55 randomly selected Grade 4 pupils, with data gathered through validated researcher-made questionnaires and analyzed using mean scores and Pearson’s product–moment correlation coefficient. Results showed that values integration was practiced at a high internalization level across dimensions: behavioral (M = 4.41, SD = 0.73), emotional (M = 4.25, SD = 0.89), and social (M = 4.40, SD = 0.75). Empathy (M = 4.38, SD = 0.71) and cooperation (M = 4.45, SD = 0.67) were rated at a very high level. A strong, positive, statistically significant relationship was found (r = 0.76, p < 0.001). While this study cannot establish causation, the strong correlation indicates that pupils who perceived stronger values integration tended to demonstrate higher empathy and cooperation.

title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells
abstractText: Abstract Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate–urea–lysine (Glu–urea–Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This study integrated molecular docking, long-timescale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and in vitro PSMA inhibition assays to assess whether the incorporation of AO or TPP disrupts the canonical PSMA binding in DOTA-based conjugates containing the Glu–urea–Lys binding motif designed by our group. Results: Docking analyses indicated that our PSMA-targeted conjugates carrying AO or TPP moieties adopt poses analogous to those of PSMA’s natural substrate N-acetyl-aspartyl-glutamate (NAAG) and of the reference conjugate natIn-PSMA-617, preserving crucial interactions within the arginine-rich S1 pocket and within the glutamate-sensing S1′ pocket. In contrast, their congeners lacking the Glu–urea–Lys binding motif exhibited surface-associated binding but failed to engage stably within the active site of PSMA. MD simulations confirmed the structural stability of the PSMA-conjugate complexes. In vitro inhibition assays supported these observations: the non-PSMA-targeted natIn-AO and natIn-TPP displayed negligible inhibitory activity against PSMA (with noncalculable IC50 values), whereas the dual-target conjugates displayed potency in the submicromolar range. Conclusion: Collectively, our results show that the dual-target conjugates recognize the PSMA protein, with subcellular targeting motifs influencing peripheral dynamics, but not core binding. This framework supports the rational design of multifunctional PSMA-directed radioconjugates for improved subcellular delivery of theranostic radionuclides toward alternative In PCa imaging and management.

title: Tailoring Alginate Encapsulates for Agricultural Biostimulants
abstractText: Abstract Alginate hydrogels have attracted considerable interest as carriers for agricultural biofertilizers due to their ability to protect and retain bioactive compounds. In this study, alginate encapsulates containing tomato green pomace and liquid fractions of fermented Ascophyllum nodosum were produced by ionic gelation and characterized using rheological, osmometric, and swelling analyses. The influence of alginate concentration, biofertilizer type, fermentation duration, and suspending medium on encapsulate behavior was investigated. All formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, while the incorporation of powdered tomato pomace and liquid fractions of fermented seaweed promoted stronger structural interactions within the silica fume suspending medium, resulting in higher viscosities than the corresponding unloaded encapsulates. The extended fermentation of A. nodosum further modified the physicochemical properties of the formulations and increased their resistance to flow. Although alginate encapsulates exhibited similar osmotic properties, swelling measurements revealed differences in network density and cross-linking, highlighting the dominant role of hydrogel architecture in determining encapsulate performance. These findings advance current knowledge on alginate-based encapsulation of agricultural biofertilizers and support the rational design of hydrogel carriers with tailored hydration, transport, and mechanical properties for agricultural applications.

title: Reverse Engineering and Shape Acquisition Technologies: A Comprehensive Review
abstractText: Reverse Engineering (RE) provides a route from an existing physical component to a digital model that can support inspection, redesign, reproduction and remanufacture. The reliability of this route depends strongly on the method used to acquire the component geometry, yet the available technologies differ markedly in measurement principle, achievable accuracy, acquisition rate, cost, surface sensitivity and geometric accessibility. This review examines shape-acquisition technologies for component-oriented RE and follows the workflow from geometric capture through point-cloud processing and mesh generation to CAD reconstruction. The literature considered includes photogrammetry, tactile coordinate measuring machines (CMMs), computed tomography (CT), structured-light scanning and laser triangulation, together with developments in automated processing and scan-to-CAD reconstruction. The review considers acquisition and reconstruction as a single engineering workflow, comparing the principal acquisition routes against common practical criteria and relating their performance to the subsequent requirements of CAD reconstruction, including recent automated and AI-assisted approaches. Its principal conceptual contribution is to clarify how acquisition decisions propagate through data quality, reconstruction effort, metrological validation and final model usability, providing a task- and traceability-oriented basis for reverse-engineering workflow selection. The comparative evidence shows that method selection is application-dependent rather than hierarchical. Tactile CMMs provide high metrological confidence but are comparatively slow for dense freeform acquisition. Photogrammetry offers low-cost and scalable capture, although its performance deteriorates on texture-poor and optically difficult surfaces. CT uniquely provides volumetric access to internal geometry but entails substantial equipment, reconstruction and uncertainty-management requirements. Structured-light and laser-triangulation systems provide faster external-surface acquisition, with different sensitivities to surface optical properties and referencing conditions. The review therefore identifies acquisition-method selection and the subsequent conversion of measured data into engineering-ready CAD geometry as the two principal determinants of RE efficiency and reliability.

Analysis of Geometric Transformations in Automatic Door System Response with a Motion Sensor
abstractText: Automatic sliding doors are usually studied as electronic systems, yet their motion offers a concrete context for geometric transformations. This study analyses how translation, reflection, and dilation describe the motion of a two-panel automatic sliding door at the main entrance of a shopping mall in Cirebon, Indonesia. The door was observed in 12 sessions over four days, with approximately 10–15 opening–closing cycles recorded per session, and the panel positions and opening widths were documented on video and mapped onto a Cartesian plane. Each panel moved by a pure horizontal translation along its rail, and the translations of the two panels were reflection-symmetric about the vertical centre line of the doorway. The representative opening width was 30 cm for a single user, 75 cm for two to three users, and 100 cm for a crowd. Taking the single-user opening as the reference aperture, the larger openings correspond to dilation factors k = 2.50 and k = 3.33 about the centre of the door, while the panels themselves remain rigid. Because detection distance and the number of users varied together and the door’s control logic was not accessible, these factors describe the observed openings rather than the controller’s rule. The door thus illustrates a composition of isometries combined with a change of scale of the aperture and can serve as a contextual resource for teaching geometric transformations.

title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research
abstractText: Abstract MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data and AI-assisted knowledge services for plant miRNA research. PmiREN3.0 is available at https://pmiren.com/.

title: L-Threonine production from acetate by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum using a pH-controlled fed-batch process
abstractText: Abstract Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon source with Corynebacterium glutamicum by integrating rational, genome-based metabolic engineering with pH-coupled fed-batch cultivation. The engineered strain AT-3 carried five chromosomal mutations that alleviated feedback inhibition of key enzymes and redirected carbon flux toward the aspartate pathway. Substrate supply was controlled using a custom Visual Basic-based feeding script that automatically adjusted the acetic acid feed in response to online pH measurements. Robust process performance was maintained during a tenfold scale-up from 100-mL DASbox to 1-L DASGIP bioreactors. The optimized process achieved an L-threonine titer of 10.04 g/L and a yield of 0.086 g/g acetate. This study provides a basis for further studies on the development and improvement of acetate-based amino acid production process. Key points • Plasmid-free C. glutamicum strains produce L-threonine in acetate minimal medium • pH-controlled acetic acid feed in bioreactors improved L-threonine production • Acetate-based production of feed amino acids avoids competition with human food

title: Comparative transcriptome analysis reveals candidate genes and defence pathways associated with resistance to potato cyst nematodes in potato (Solanum tuberosum)
abstractText: Globodera rostochiensis and Globodera pallida are two nematode species responsible for are potato cyst nematode (PCN) that significantly reduce potato (Solanum tuberosum) productivity worldwide. To elucidate the molecular basis of PCN resistance, we compared transcriptomic responses of the highly resistant potato breeding clone SM/11-120 with the susceptible cultivar Kufri Jyoti following simultaneous infection with both PCN species. Nematode penetration assays showed that SM/11-120 completely restricted nematode invasion up to 7 days post-inoculation (dpi), whereas Kufri Jyoti was susceptible to nematode penetration within 24 h post-inoculation (hpi) and supported juvenile development at 72 hpi and 7 dpi. RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq) generated 18–27 million high-quality paired-end reads per library, of which 51.6–68.3% mapped uniquely to the potato reference genome. Comparative transcriptome analysis identified 724, 795, 694, and 899 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SM/11-120 and Kufri Jyoti at 0 hpi, 24 hpi, 72 hpi, and 7 dpi, respectively. The resistant genotype exhibited enhanced expression of genes involved in immune signalling (NRC1, NBS-LRR), transcriptional regulation (WRKY, MYB), calcium signalling, pathogenesis-related proteins (PR1), hormone and defence metabolism (ACO1, geraniol 10-hydroxylase), and cell wall reinforcement (HRGP, XTH3, pectinesterase, β-expansin). Gene Ontology analysis revealed stronger enrichment of stress response, biological regulation, nitrogen compound metabolism, and response to biotic stimulus in SM/11-120 than in Kufri Jyoti. Expression patterns of selected defence-related genes were validated by quantitative reverse transcription (qRT)-PCR, confirming their rapid and sustained induction in the resistant genotype.

title: Exercise intensity and all-cause mortality among individuals with and without lung cancer: a nationwide propensity score-matched cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Objective Lung cancer is associated with high mortality, and emerging evidence suggests that physical activity may improve survival outcomes. However, the influence of exercise intensity on all-cause mortality among individuals with lung cancer compared with a matched non-cancer comparison cohort remains unclear. This study examined the association between exercise intensity and mortality in a large, propensity score–matched cohort of Korean adults with and without lung cancer. Methods We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service. Of 1,134,909 individuals in the source cohort, the final propensity score–matched analytic cohort included 7,296 participants: 3,648 individuals with lung cancer and 3,648 J00 non-cancer comparison participants. Associations between exercise intensity and all-cause mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusting for measured demographic, behavioral, laboratory, and comorbidity-related covariates. Survival differences according to lung cancer status and exercise intensity were examined using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results Reporting vigorous-intensity activity on at least one day per week was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality compared with reporting no moderate- or vigorous-intensity activity. In multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, any reported vigorous-intensity activity was associated with a lower hazard of death (HR = 0.734, 95% CI: 0.666–0.809; p < 0.0001) after adjustment for measured demographic, behavioral, laboratory, and comorbidity-related covariates. Higher CCI was also associated with increased mortality risk. Conclusions Self-reported activity category was associated with all-cause mortality in this matched nationwide cohort. However, because the primary analysis was conducted in the overall matched cohort and cancer stage, histological subtype, treatment modality, and performance status were unavailable, residual confounding and reverse causation cannot be excluded. These findings should be interpreted as observational associations rather than lung cancer-specific or causal effects. Prospective studies incorporating detailed cancer-specific clinical information and more comprehensive physical activity assessment are warranted.

title: Modulating Sulfur Composition toward Ultralow Dielectric Loss Polymers: A Miscible Blending Strategy with Poly(phenylene oxide)/Poly(phenylene sulfide) Alternating Copolymers
abstractText: Abstract In recent high-speed communications (i.e., 5G and 6G), insulating polymers exhibiting both a minimized dielectric constant (Dk) and dissipation factor (Df) have been extensively used to reduce dielectric loss, although the empirical Dk–Df trade-off relationship has prevented further reductions in these values. Here, we describe a rational approach for the simultaneous reduction of both Dk and Df through simple polymer blending, wherein a low-Dk ether polymer is hybridized with a low-Df sulfide polymer. Specifically, upon mixing poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene sulfide) (PMPS) or poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO) with their alternating copolymer, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms of the resulting polymer blends revealed their miscibility, as verified by shifting of glass-transition temperatures, allowing for the successful film preparation and the tuning of their dielectric properties without compromising other material properties (e.g., thermostability). In particular, the observed enhancement in free fractional volume for the polymer blends suggests a reduction in Dk, finally minimizing dielectric loss (Dk = 2.43, Df = 0.00081 at 10 GHz). Specifically, those dielectric losses are significantly lower than the empirical limits defined for single-component polymers. Overall, this study describes a rational strategy for the preparation of diverse insulating polymers with extremely low dielectric losses.

title: Bridging laboratory and clinical practice: timelines and challenges in wet lab research
abstractText: For surgical trainees embarking on a period of laboratory research, the transition from operating theatre to bench science can be both rewarding and disorienting. This annotation is written specifically for clinicians entering a wet laboratory environment, typically on an out-of-programme research placement, who may be unfamiliar with the realities of experimental science. Drawing on the first-hand experiences of a multidisciplinary orthopaedic research team, it explains why laboratory timelines are often longer than expected, and offers practical guidance for working effectively alongside PhD-level scientists, postdoctoral researchers, research technicians, and their trainees – collaborators whose technical expertise is indispensable to experimental success. Wet lab work involves complex protocols, tissue handling, assay optimization, and regulatory approvals, all of which can significantly extend project timelines. Effective communication, realistic planning, and mutual respect are crucial to manage unforeseen challenges and ensure that experiments are reliable, reproducible, and clinically meaningful. Menopausal hormone therapy and frailty risk: a nationwide Korean target trial emulation study
abstractText: Abstract Background Menopause is associated with functional decline, but evidence linking menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) to frailty risk remains limited. Aims To evaluate whether achievement of a prespecified MHT exposure threshold was associated with lower frailty risk among MHT initiators. Methods Using the NHIS-HEALS database (2002–2019), we conducted a nationwide new-user cohort study of 31,294 women aged ≥ 45 years who initiated systemic MHT and were non-frail at baseline, with up to 10 years of follow-up. The outcome was transition to high frailty risk status (Hospital Frailty Risk Score [HFRS] > 15). The target strategy was ≥ 28 cumulative days of MHT within 60 days of initiation. Strategies were compared by clone–censor–weighting within a target trial emulation framework, with doubly robust estimation. Results Overall, 25,907 participants (82.8%) achieved the target strategy, which was associated with a lower risk of transition (aHR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.85–0.92; adjusted 10-year risk difference, − 3.7%; 95% CI, − 4.7 to − 2.8). The association was more pronounced among women aged ≥ 50 years and those with intermediate baseline frailty risk (HFRS 5–15; aHR, 0.77), and differed by formulation (tibolone, aHR 0.63; estrogen-only therapy, aHR 0.94). Discussion The outcome was based on a claims-derived frailty risk score, and because both groups comprised MHT initiators, the findings reflect early adherence rather than MHT use versus non-use. Conclusions Achievement of the specific early MHT exposure threshold was associated with lower transition to high frailty risk status.

Association of electrical properties of bioelectrical impedance spectroscopy with sedentary time, physical activity and muscle function in older adults
abstractText: Abstract Introduction Little is known about the relationship between cell health indicators measured by the bioelectrical impedance spectroscopy (BIS) electrical properties such as phase angle (PhA), characteristic frequency ( f c ), and membrane capacitance ( C m ) and objective indicators of sedentary time, physical activity levels, and muscle function among older adults. This study examined the BIS parameters and their association with sedentary time, physical activity, and muscle function. Methods Data from 96 older adults were used. The BIS electrical properties, physical activity, grip strength, short physical performance battery (SPPB), and timed-up-and-go (TUG) were assessed, after which multiple regression analyses were conducted. Results The findings showed that individuals with normal phase angle (PhA) scores exhibited greater light physical activity, daily activity counts, grip strength, and SPPB scores compared to those with low PhA. PhA and membrane capacitance ( C m ) showed a negative correlation with sedentary time and TUG and a positive correlation with low physical activity, grip strength, and SPPB. The characteristic frequency ( f c ) was positively correlated with sedentary time and negatively correlated with low physical activity and grip strength. Multiple regression analyses showed that only PhA was the significant predictor of sedentary time, low physical activity, total activity counts per day, SPPB, and TUG. Conclusion Results suggest that PhA may serve as a useful adjunctive indicator of physical activity and functional status among older adults.

Obstructive hydrocephalus due to posterior third ventricle pathology: One or two burr hole approaches for ETV and biopsy
abstractText: Abstract Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) and tumor biopsy is a frequent procedure for third ventricular tumors. While some authors favor one approach to achieve both goals, others support the selection of two approaches to avoid fornical damage and venous hemorrhage. Here the authors present their experience with both techniques. A retrospective analysis was conducted on cases which underwent an ETV and a tumor procedure in lesions of the posterior third ventricle from 2011 to 2025. Patient records, pre- and postoperative imaging and intraoperative video recordings were retrospectively analyzed. Twenty-six patients met the inclusion criteria: 13 were treated with one, the other 13 with two approaches. The surgical goal of ETV and tumor biopsy/resection was achieved in all cases. No procedure was abandoned. No postoperative complication was observed. Intraoperative forniceal injury was observed in 8/26 patients (31%). Intraoperative bleeding was found in 81% (21/26 cases). In 19% of cases (5/26 cases), intraoperative bleeding required a longer irrigation time but no switch to dry field technique or open surgery was needed. On follow up, three patients required ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement. Thus, ETV success scored 88.5% (23/26 cases). On 2D MRI, the mean intertrajectory angle was smaller in the one-burr-hole group than in the two-burr-hole group (41.8° ± 3.5° vs. 48.7° ± 5.4°; p = 0.001). Lesions of the posterior third ventricle causing obstructive hydrocephalus are ideal candidates for an endoscopic approach. The overall success rate is very high with acceptable surgical risks. In this cohort, larger intertrajectory angles were associated with selection of a two-burr-hole approach. The approximate 45° value was derived post hoc and requires external validation.

Legal Ethics of Generative Artificial Intelligence Training Data Usage in Large Language Models: Copyright and Personal Data Perspective
abstractText: This research originates from security and privacy risks associated with Generative AI Large Language Models (LLMs), especially concerning data used for training in relation to Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and Personal Data Protection (PDP). The study seeks to examine existing regulatory guidance and develop a national framework that protects user privacy and IPR. The method employs normative legal research using statutory and conceptual approaches, by reviewing the legal frameworks of Indonesia, South Korea, the European Union (EU), and Japan, along with direct testing of LLM prompts. The findings show that LLMs continuously absorb users’ input prompts, data, and corrections to support deeper model training, thereby revealing significant security vulnerabilities under PDP laws. Moreover, in the absence of strong human creative control and predictability, each incoming data item may potentially breach privacy and copyright laws and may also damage original creators. Therefore, legal governance should move toward explicit licensing, fair compensation, and technical verification standards such as provenance labeling. The study concludes that mandatory human-centric supervision, explicit user consent, and freedom of choice are essential legal limits. Ultimately, effective AI governance depends on a shared responsibility model: software engineers must implement technical transparency, expert oversight, and responsive complaint mechanisms, while end users must select platforms lawfully, comply strictly with output licensing requirements, and actively monitor the system.

title: CONVEXITY WITH SOFT APPROXIMATE FUNCTION UNDER FUZZY SOFT EXPERT SET ENVIRONMENT
abstractText: Soft set theory is considered the best tool to deal with problems involving uncertainties by controlling all the complexities of optimization theory, fuzzy set theory, and probability theory. By utilising this theory, the majority of soft set-like models have been developed to address issues in decision-making and medical diagnosis with a single expert. This is a challenge for researchers who employ questionnaires. This issue is solved by soft expert sets, which enable the decision-maker to access the opinions of all experts in a single model. In this study, some types of convexity, like strictly (strongly) convexity, (λ,ψ)-convexity with different senses over fuzzy soft expert set, have been described with the numerical examples. Convex hull and convex cone on fuzzy soft expert set have been developed, and some important results have been proved by applying the algebraic approach

title: Case-Based Learning, Class Attendance, And Academic Achievement of Master of Management Students In A Human Resource Performance Planning and Appraisal Course
abstractText: This study evaluates the academic achievement of Master of Management students in a Human Resource Performance Planning and Appraisal course after the second half of the semester was redesigned around case-based and problem-based learning, and examines how attendance and assessment components relate to final grades. A descriptive-retrospective quantitative design was applied to the complete institutional records of all 29 students in one class at Universitas Islam Sumatera Utara, Indonesia, in the odd semester of the 2024/2025 academic year. Descriptive statistics, normality tests, Pearson and Spearman correlations, and paired t-tests were applied. The mean final grade was 83.78 (SD 5.30), all students passed, and 48.28% obtained an A. Attendance averaged 95.57% and correlated strongly with the mean of the academic components that exclude attendance (r = 0.874; ρ = 0.844; p < 0.001). Final project scores, obtained after the case-based phase, exceeded mid-term scores by 1.72 points (t(28) = 3.27; p = 0.003; dz = 0.61), and 19 of the 29 students improved. All four course learning outcomes were attained. The findings suggest that case-based learning suits working postgraduate students and that attendance is a strong marker of engagement, although the single-group retrospective design does not permit causal inference.

title: Management-changing diagnosis of presumed clamp-related brachiocephalic artery injury by transesophageal echocardiography during total aortic arch replacement: a case report
abstractText: Abstract Background Aortic arch branch malperfusion during total aortic arch replacement requires prompt diagnosis. We report a case in which transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) clarified discordant intraoperative monitoring findings and directly guided surgical revision. Case presentation A 77-year-old woman underwent total aortic arch replacement. After separation from cardiopulmonary bypass, right radial arterial pressure and right regional cerebral oxygen saturation markedly decreased, whereas direct brachiocephalic arterial pressure remained preserved. Targeted TEE demonstrated brachiocephalic artery dissection extending into the right common carotid artery with true-lumen compression, loss of antegrade flow into the right subclavian artery, and retrograde vertebral collateral flow. These findings prompted immediate surgical revision. After reconstruction, arterial pressure and cerebral oxygen saturation recovered, and TEE confirmed restoration of antegrade flow. Conclusions Targeted TEE can clarify discordant monitoring findings in aortic arch branch malperfusion and provide critical information for intraoperative surgical decision-making.

title: O prazer e o sofrimento psíquico do trabalho na saúde mental dos estagiários: um olhar da Psicodinâmica do trabalho
abstractText: As transformações no mundo do trabalho ao longo dos séculos intensificaram a competitividade e as adversidades enfrentadas pelos trabalhadores, tornando essencial compreender os impactos dessas dinâmicas na saúde mental. Neste contexto, o presente estudo adotou a Psicodinâmica do Trabalho como referencial teórico, por analisar a relação subjetiva entre trabalhador e atividade laboral a partir das vivências de prazer e sofrimento, indicadores fundamentais de saúde ou adoecimento. Considerando a escassez de estudos que aplicam essa abordagem especificamente ao público de estagiários, o objetivo desta pesquisa foi analisar os indicadores de prazer e sofrimento no trabalho entre estagiários de diferentes áreas. A abordagem foi quantitativa, envolvendo 35 participantes, e utilizou como instrumento a Escala de Indicadores de Prazer e Sofrimento no Trabalho (EIPST), integrante do Inventário de Trabalho e Risco de Adoecimento Relacionado ao Trabalho (ITRA). Os resultados revelaram que as maiores fontes de prazer estão associadas ao orgulho pelo trabalho realizado e à liberdade para dialogar sobre suas atividades com colegas. Contudo, as vivências de sofrimento mostraram-se mais intensas e frequentes, destacando-se indicadores como esgotamento emocional, estresse, sobrecarga, frustração e insegurança. Conclui-se que, no grupo pesquisado, os achados indicam predominância do sofrimento em relação ao prazer, apontando para sinais que merecem atenção quanto à saúde mental e reforçando a importância de ambientes de aprendizagem mais saudáveis. Além disso, os dados fornecem subsídios para futuras investigações sobre a experiência dos estagiários no contexto laboral.

Low-Temperature Limit of Spontaneous Polarization in BaTiO 3 Determined Using a (111)-Oriented Single Crystal
abstractText: The spontaneous polarization of BaTiO 3 has long served as a standard in ferroelectric physics; however, its low-temperature limit has not been determined experimentally. In this study, we directly measured the spontaneous polarization of a BaTiO 3 single crystal cut into a (111)-oriented plate through pyroelectric charge measurements under field-cooling conditions. The polarization increased monotonically upon cooling and reached at least 32 µC/cm 2 at 0 K, consistent with the Berry-phase based first-principles predictions.

title: Mechanisms of transcriptional activation and repression by dual plant salicylic acid receptors
abstractText: Abstract For two decades, NPR1 (Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis-Related Genes 1; also called NIM1) has been known as a transcriptional activator of systemic acquired resistance in plants. NPR1 and its paralogs NPR3/NPR4 serve as dual receptors of salicylic acid (SA). Nevertheless, how NPR1 engages TGA transcription factors to recruit RNA polymerase II and initiate transcription has remained unresolved. Recent work identified Mediator complex subunit 15A (MED15A) as a bridge that couples NPR1 to the Mediator complex, and SA directly promotes NPR1–MED15A interaction, which is crucial for NPR1-mediated transcriptional activation. Meanwhile, NIM1-interacting protein 1 (NIMIN1) binds NPR3/NPR4 and the Topless (TPL) corepressors, connecting NPR3/NPR4 to Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2)-mediated chromatin repression. SA disrupts the NPR3/NPR4–NIMIN1 interaction, reducing H3K27 trimethylation, increasing histone H3 acetylation at SA-responsive genes, thereby relieving NPR3/NPR4-mediated repression. These new discoveries unravel the mechanistic framework for how SA perception triggers transcriptional reprogramming and offer strategies for designing more effective SA analogs as agrochemicals to enhance crop disease resistance.

title: Orbital-Enabled Intrinsic Defect Healing via Charge Compensation toward Accelerated Sodium Storage in Mn-Rich Composite Phosphates
abstractText: Abstract Manganese-rich composite phosphate cathodes, represented by Na4Fe1.25Mn1.75(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP), offer high energy density for sodium-ion batteries. However, their limited electrochemical durability and sluggish kinetics hinder practical application. In this work, we first identify abundant intrinsic oxygen vacancies, which are determined to be responsible for the occurrence of Mn/Na antisite defects and deteriorate electrochemical performance of NFMPP. Building on the new insight, we design a trace V-doped Mn-rich composite phosphate cathode, Na4Fe1.25Mn1.65V0.1(PO4)2P2O7 (NFMPP-V). Different from other dopants (Cr3+, Co2+, Ni2+, Nb5+), the unique empty eg*0 orbitals and modest charge compensation (Δz = +1) of V3+ effectively reduce the oxygen-vacancy defects in the NFMPP structure. This reduction leads to a more uniform strain distribution and a lower concentration of in situ formed Mn/Na anti-site defects, ultimately accelerating Na+ kinetics and enabling more complete utilization of the intrinsic low-voltage Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reaction. Consequently, NFMPP-V can deliver an energy density of 421.1 Wh/kg, relating to a reversible capacity of 125.7 mAh g–1 with an enhanced initial Coulombic efficiency of 97.0% (105.8 mAh g–1, 87.0% for the NFMPP), outperforming most Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes reported to date. Notably, a full pouch cell paired with a hard-carbon anode retains 93.6% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. This work clarifies the decisive role of oxygen-vacancy defects in Mn-rich composite phosphate cathodes and provides a new insight for developing high-performance sodium-ion batteries.

title: Students’ Interaction Patterns with ChatGPT in Solving Image-Based Mathematics Problems
abstractText: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT are increasingly used by students to obtain explanations and solutions to mathematics problems. However, access to answers does not necessarily mean that students examine the underlying reasoning. This study aimed to describe students’ interaction patterns with ChatGPT when solving image-based mathematics problems, variations in these patterns across two problems, and how students responded to, sought clarification of, or challenged ChatGPT-generated solutions. A qualitative descriptive design was employed. The participants were Grade 9 students of one intact class (total sampling), and the records of 31 students who worked on two image-based problems, concerning the area of a trapezoidal footpath and the painted area of a photo frame, were analyzed. The primary data consisted of student–ChatGPT conversation transcripts exported from shared conversation links. The transcripts were analyzed descriptively and qualitatively using six predefined interaction patterns: requesting a solution and then ending the interaction; seeking clarification; requesting a re-explanation; checking an answer or testing a method; following a solution step by step; and connecting or redirecting the interaction. The unit of analysis was the student–problem episode, and overlapping codes were permitted. The findings indicate that students did more than request answers. Some asked for the rationale behind a solution step, proposed strategies for confirmation, requested further explanations, responded to practice questions posed by ChatGPT, and made connections between the two problems. Two students questioned the complexity or necessity of ChatGPT’s chosen method. Differences between the problems were primarily reflected in the content of students’ questions. These findings are descriptive and are not intended to establish the prevalence of interaction patterns, learning outcomes, or causal relationships. The findings suggest a need for task design and teacher guidance that encourage students to verify and evaluate AI-generated solutions.

Masseter ultrasonographic characteristics across clinically defined groups of antidepressant users and non-user controls: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Masseter ultrasonographic characteristics remain incompletely described in antidepressant users with differing clinical bruxism classifications. This study compared three predefined clinical groups. Methods This single-center cross-sectional study used prospectively acquired clinical and imaging data from 123 adults: antidepressant users with clinically defined probable bruxism and a self-reported temporal association (G1, n = 42), antidepressant users without probable bruxism (G2, n = 31), and non-antidepressant controls without probable bruxism (G3, n = 50). For G1, recalled onset or worsening of bruxism-related complaints after treatment initiation was recorded during anamnesis; this chronology was entirely retrospective. Bilateral thickness, estimated volume, and a reciprocal strain-elastography metric were measured at rest and during voluntary clenching; fractal dimension was calculated from resting images. Nonparametric comparisons, adjusted regression models, and secondary inter-parameter correlations were performed. Results G1 had higher resting and clenching thickness, estimated volume, reciprocal strain-elastography values, and resting fractal dimension than G2 and G3. Thickness, estimated volume, and the reciprocal strain-elastography metric increased from rest to clench in all groups. Between-group differences remained statistically evident in models adjusted for the measured covariates. Conclusions Masseter ultrasound-derived measurements differed among the predefined clinical groups. These findings do not establish the onset or progression of bruxism, a causal effect of antidepressant use, or a medication-specific muscle phenotype.

Chemical Regulation of Multiscale Crack Healing in Cementitious Materials by Active Components of Crystalline Admixtures
abstractText: Abstract Crystalline admixtures facilitate crack self-healing in cementitious materials via precipitation and ion migration, yet the specific chemical roles of individual active components remain poorly understood, limiting insight into the underlying healing mechanisms. To address this issue, sodium carbonate, sodium silicate, and calcium formate were selected as representative active components of crystalline admixtures and comparatively investigated through single-component analysis. The self-healing behavior of mortar was evaluated based on crack width evolution, relative water flow ratio, compressive strength retention, chloride migration coefficient, pore structure characteristics, and the structure and composition of healing products. The results indicated that all three functional admixtures promoted crack healing by inducing precipitation reactions, while exhibiting distinct roles at different scales. Sodium silicate showed the most pronounced effect on internal microcrack healing and pore structure refinement. After preloading and curing, the compressive strength retention of mortar containing sodium silicate increased to 90.4%, and the chloride migration coefficient decreased to 5.43 × 10–12 m2/s, accompanied by a noticeable reduction in large pores. In contrast, calcium formate performed better in macroscopic crack closure. Mortar incorporating calcium formate achieved complete healing of cracks with dimensions between 0.10 and 0.36 mm, while the relative water flow ratio decreased to 4.8% and the cumulative water absorption was decreased by 35.4% compared with the ordinary mortar. XRD analysis identified CaCO3 as a major crystalline phase in the crack regions. The incorporation of functional admixtures led to a more continuous and denser deposition layer, among which calcium formate formed a more intact healing layer at the crack surface, contributing to more stable crack closure.

title: Analisis Penerimaan Pengguna Fitur "Orang Asli Papua" pada Aplikasi Identitas Kependudukan Digital Menggunakan Technology Acceptance Model
abstractText: The Indigenous Papuan (OAP) feature in the Digital Population Identity (IKD) application was developed to support Papua's Special Autonomy through the digitalization of population administration services. However, its utilization is hindered by low digital literacy and limited internet access. This study aims to analyze the acceptance of the OAP feature among Indigenous Papuan communities in Manokwari Regency using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). A quantitative approach was employed, involving 175 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected via a Google Forms-based questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that Perceived Ease of Use positively influences both Behavioral Intention and Perceived Usefulness, ultimately encouraging public acceptance of the OAP feature in the IKD application.

title: Autoconstrucción frente a contratación externa de invernaderos geodésicos: Análisis de escenarios de costo para agricultura protegida
abstractText: The initial cost of the structure limits the adoption of protected agriculture among smallholders. This study estimated how the projected price of a 10 m diameter V3 geodesic structure changes from self-construction to external contracting, and which assumptions drive the difference. A layered price model (direct cost, overheads, contingencies, profit and value-added tax) was applied to three direct-cost scenarios: the reported budget (MXN 16,556.00), a corrected cutting plan of 68 steel profiles, and an additional per-worker labour correction. The original contractor budget was reconciled, margin on sales was compared with markup on cost, and a one-way sensitivity analysis, a 20,000-run Monte Carlo simulation and a scope threshold against a MXN 600/m² conventional reference were computed. The profit line of the original table (MXN 4,139.00) equals a 25% markup on direct cost, not the profit used in the subtotal (MXN 4,759.85). The contractor price was 1.67 times the self-construction cost in every scenario; profit (43.1%) and VAT (34.5%) account for most of the gap. With the corrections, the contractor price rises from 351.50 to 472.69 MXN/m² of base area; the simulated median is 457.9 MXN/m² (P5–P95: 375.7–549.6). The comparison with conventional greenhouses holds only if excluded items cost less than MXN 10,000–19,500. All scenarios are simulated, not field observations.

title: Sulfur Vacancy-Engineered ZnIn2S4 Nanosheets Integrated with CoS1.097 for Enhanced Visible Light-Driven Nitrogen Photofixation
abstractText: Abstract Herein, S-scheme heterojunction photocatalysts integrating sulfur vacancy-engineered ZnIn2S4 (Sv-ZnInS) with CoS1.097 (CoS) were successfully synthesized via a simple hydrothermal reaction. The formed CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterostructures exhibited considerably high catalytic activity toward visible light-driven photocatalytic nitrogen (N2) fixation. Notably, the optimized 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS sample achieved an ammonia yield of 18.18 ± 0.39 mg·L–1 after 1 h of visible-light illumination, which was an approximately 2.4-fold enhancement relative to pristine Sv-ZnInS. The S-scheme charge separation and transfer pathway was elucidated via in situ irradiated X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, noble-metal loading, and band structure analysis. The underlying N2 photofixation mechanism was systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy. The results revealed that N2 photofixation over the 3CoS/Sv-ZnInS catalyst occurred via a multistep proton-coupled electron transfer. Our findings indicate that S-scheme CoS/Sv-ZnInS heterojunctions may offer a viable route toward visible light-driven photocatalytic N2 fixation.
